It was not just a city of powerful beings; it was a city of true believers!
They do not just think they are superior; they know it, with a certainty that is as fundamental as their own breathing!
And that belief, that collective, indefatigable certainty, is a weapon more potent than any army, a shield more resilient than any wall.
For in the end, the wars of existence are not won by those with the most power, but by those with the most absolute, unshakeable, and glorious faith in their own, chosen truth.
At this time...
"My friends, look upon those who seek to disrupt our Way of Existence."
The voice of Forgemaster Vulcan echoed out nearby with calm and glory as he smiled while nodding to the far distance.
He was on the rampart, his massive form a silent, bronze mountain of contained power.
Around him, other Elder Early Creatures, beings whose very presence was a law of nature, stood in a loose, yet perfectly coordinated formation.
Their gazes were fixed on the horizon, but their demeanor was not one of fear.
It was... a quiet, almost leisurely, anticipation.
As if they were waiting for a storm they knew they could weather.
Noah also looked ahead.
His eyes, now capable of perceiving the very texture of reality, saw it.
Light-years away, a storm of complexity and purity was surging towards them.
It was not a chaotic, natural phenomenon.
It was an army.
And as the distance closed, as the light of their approach finally resolved into discernible shapes, Noah's gaze, and the very core of his being, buzzed gloriously at what he saw!
Tens of thousands of them.
Justiciars!
'In such a short period of time?'
He shook his head in amazement as a fee things here didnt make sense!
But there they were!
Their pristine white armor, a stark, brutalist mockery of the elegant, growth-type Aegis he wore, gleamed with a cold, sterile light.
They moved in perfect, silent unison, a river of absolute, unyielding Purity that threatened to wash away all that stood in its path.
|Hostile Force Composition Analyzed.|
|Primary Threat: [Living Existential Armor – Justiciar Model].|
|Quantity: Approximately 30,000 units observed so far.|
|Power Range: 800 Quadrillion (Standard Infantry) to 1,500 Quadrillion (Elite Guard).|
HUUM!
At the very forefront of this terrifying legion, a small, yet infinitely more dangerous, contingent floated.
They were the commanders, the architects of this coming war.
Noah's gaze settled on the central figure, and his interface provided a name that was a quiet, terrible detonation in his mind.
|[Dr.
Flamel]|
|Classification: Elder Early Creature|
|Complexity: 3,200 Quadrillion|
|Purity: 3,300 Quadrillion|
He was a being of impossible, terrible power, clad in a simple, pristine white lab coat that seemed to mock the very concept of armor.
Surrounding him were other beings of a similar, terrifying caliber.
Elder Early Creatures whose power exceeded 1,001 Quadrillion, their forms a diverse, magnificent pageant of primordial might.
And a few, like Vulcan, were Elder Early Creatures who had their very presence a weight that seemed to bend the fabric of the Fold.
This was not merely an army.
This was a single, collective beast of innovation, a civilization of science that had weaponized its own genius!
Noah could feel it, a collective Haki that wrapped around them all, a unified field of will that made them a single, unstoppable entity.
He could feel the cold, callous light in the eyes of the Justiciars, the absence of emotion, the pure, clinical intent to... purify.
It was eerily similar to the one from his current time!
And more than that, he could feel the vibrant, almost arrogant, glow of multiple Principles, ancient and terrible weavings of existence that wrapped around Dr.
Flamel and the others like a second skin.
The very air began to tremble with both a simple, physical shaking...and a deep, conceptual shudder!
HUUM!
Existential Trembling.
The very fabric of the First Folds groaned under the weight of so much concentrated power moving with a single, unified purpose!
Oh!
The ground beneath Aethelgard, the sky above it, the very space between its atoms... all of it began to vibrate with a terror that was absolute!
Oh!!

chapters.title: Chapter 4290 War! IV
paragraphs: But as the Existential Trembling unfolded...
HUUM!
A golden light erupted from the heart of Aethelgard!
It was not a blinding flash, but a soft, warm, and utterly absolute glow that washed over everything.
And in that instant, the trembling stopped.
The very air, which had been a screaming chorus of impending doom, became still, reinforced, and utterly, profoundly, calm.
|[A grand Principle has been exerted.]|
|Analysis: I have barely managed to decipher a sliver of its nature, Master. It appears to be [The Principle of the Sovereign's Domain].|

|Effect: Within a defined territory, the will of the Sovereign is absolute. The very laws of existence can be rewritten. In this case, the law 'Existence shall tremble before overwhelming power' has been temporarily amended to 'Existence shall not tremble, for the Sovereign finds it distracting.'|
WAA!
Noah listened to RUIN/EDEN's words, his eyes shining with a sharp, analytical light.
Who? Who had unleashed such a terrifying power, a Principle that could impose its will on Existence itself with such casual, absolute authority?
He looked around, but no one had moved.
Vulcan and the others simply smiled, their confidence now seeming less like faith and more like... knowledge.
At that moment, from the ranks of the approaching enemy, a new figure floated forward.
She was an Early Creature of terrifying power, her form clad in a fiery red chiton that did little to hide her magnificent, curvaceous figure.
And she was curveceous!
Her eyes shone with a brilliant, almost manic, light as she smiled and breathed in the surrounding air. Her voice boomed out, a glorious, theatrical declaration.
"Was that the light of The First Leader?! Sir, I am your biggest fan! Why don't you come out so we can gaze upon you?!"
|[Valkyrie Anastasia]|
|Classification: Elder Early Creature|
|Complexity: 3,800 Quadrillion|
|Purity: 3,900 Quadrillion|
The First Leader. Gilgamesh. The golden light that had just stilled a Fold-wide tremor... it was his?
Noah's eyes flashed sharply as he looked around, but nothing and nobody rose to answer the Valkyrie's call. She pouted, a gesture that was both childlike and utterly terrifying.
"It seems like you won't come out just yet... okay! I know those like you have to make a grand entrance. I shall do the honors. Ahem!"
She waved her hand, and an illusory scroll of pure, informational light materialized before her.

She began to speak, her voice now a formal, ringing proclamation. "I, Valkyrie Anastasia, Blade of the Rising Sun, stand before everyone today to announce the intent of war between The Early Laboratories and Aethelgard! This is due to the repeated and egregious invasions from Aethelgard to steal our weavings of existence, the unprovoked deaths of our esteemed researchers, and a fundamental violation of the sovereignty of the sacred Laboratories of THE Living Concept! This simply cannot be allowed to go on unchecked! That is why we stand here today. To defend... our Way of Existence that has been threatened by Aethelgard!"
HUUM!
Her voice was grand and piercing as it spread all around.
The moment it did so, Noah's own existence buzzed, a violent, protesting vibration!
The Principles within him, Cheating Architect and Perpetual Harvest, rumbled with a sudden, urgent warning.
|[CRITICAL ALERT: EXISTENTIAL THREAT DETECTED.]|

|[The Principle of the Cheating Architect] has detected the opening and collapse of countless possibilities. This conflict is a nexus event, a focal point in the weavings of existence. The level of observation on this battlefield is... absolute.|
|Analysis: There is a 90% certainty that this war is being directly observed by both [THE Living Concept] and [THE Living Spirit], and potentially multiple other Level One Scale existences.|

|Conclusion: If you, Master, an anomaly from a future epoch, are observed by any of these beings enough to garner their attention, there is a 99% certainty that your intrusion in the Earliest Folds will be discovered as they will know you do not belong. The consequences would be... catastrophic.|
Noah read the information as his existence buzzed...but he felt no Doubt!
He felt no Fear!
He had none of it to give.
But...
To be seen, to be known by a being of that scale... it was not a risk he could afford to take.
|[Strategic Re-evaluation Initiated.]|

|Primary Directive: Self-Preservation. You cannot be an active participant in this conflict. Even the acquisition of potential loot must be handled with extreme care. The risk of detection is too high.|

|Action: [The Principle of the Cheating Architect] is invoking a new protocol. Your authority as a [Protagonist] is being temporarily sealed to ensure you do not inadvertently draw the narrative focus of this event. Furthermore, Cheating Architect has activated the authority of your [Plot Tower of Osmont] to rewrite your existential signature.|
|Your new role: Background Character. A nameless, faceless extra. You will blend into the background, your presence a mere whisper in the storm.|
WAA!
He felt it. A profound, almost painful, shift in his very being.
The vibrant, tyrannical light that had always surrounded him dimmed, faded, and was replaced by a quiet, unassuming grayness.
The Glyphs on his body became invisible, their power contained. The Aegis, his glorious armor, remained a simple, unadorned necklace that radiated no authority at all.
He moved backwards, to the periphery of the Rampart, a slow, shuffling movement that was utterly unlike his usual, confident stride.
The Early Creatures around him, who had been a silent, supportive presence, did not even spare him a glance. He was no longer one of them. He was... nothing.
|[The Principle of Perpetual Harvest] has recognized the immense effort required to be a nobody. This act of self-suppression is a profound one.|
|Your ability to blend into the background is being amplified. Your presence is now conceptually... irrelevant.|
He floated in an unseen corner of the Rampart, a single, insignificant figure in a sea of titans!
He had his power, yes. He had his plans. But for now, he had to be a ghost.
He had to watch, to learn, and to survive. For the greatest battles are not always won by the strongest, but by the one who is still standing when the dust settles.
And to do that, sometimes, one must first learn the art of not being seen at all!
To be a speck of dust!
Ashes to ashes, dust to dust!

chapters.title: Chapter 4291 What is The Way? I
paragraphs: Noah melted into the background, his figure becoming a whisper in a symphony of roaring power!

Some existences went about their lives without wanting to be seen, content in their quiet corners of reality. Others, however, moved with a grace and a purpose that was a declaration in itself, a demand to be witnessed, to be admired, to be feared.
Right now, Noah was in the shadows, and from this vantage point, he watched a terrifying conflict begin in the most unexpected way possible!
After the grand, theatrical declaration from Valkyrie Anastasia, the battlefield fell into a profound, anticipatory silence.
She floated there, a fiery jewel against the dark canvas of the First Folds, her gaze fixed on the distant, golden walls of Aethelgard.
A piercing smile touched her lips, an expression of pure, unadulterated confidence.
This was not a war to her. It was a game.
But it was not a fucking game!
|System Analysis Initiating: [The War for Aethelgard].|
|Primary Combatants:|
| - [The Gilgamesh Sovereignty]: Offensive Force. Primary strength lies in the widespread implementation of the [Principles], [Living Astral Codex] system, [Glyphs]...|
| - [The Early Laboratories]: Attacking Force. Primary strength lies in the mass-produced [Living Existential Armor – Justiciar Model], [Principles], [Glyphs]...|
And the battle had truly begun!
Because in the next moment, hidden in the shadows of his own, self-imposed obscurity, Noah's eyes, now windows of pure, analytical data, captured an event of impossible, terrible beauty.
On the Rampart of Aethelgard, the Elder Early Creatures, beings like Forgemaster Vulcan whose very presence was a law of nature, moved as one.
It was not a coordinated attack, but a symphony of synchronized, absolute will!
Their hands rose in unison, and from the very fabric of their beings, a new, brilliant light bloomed from their Grimoires!
HUUM!
They were activating their Living Astral Codexes!
It was a glorious, terrifying sight.
Above the heads of fifteen of these ancient titans, illusory Astral Arcana Glyphs materialized, each one a shimmering, conceptual card of pure, ordered light.
They were windows into different, impossible realities, each depicting a unique wonder, a different instrument of destruction.
Some were identical, a testament to a shared arsenal, a common, terrible tool in their collective toolbox.
|Fifteen [Astral Arcana Glyphs] have been activated simultaneously.|
|Rarity Assessment: All Glyphs appear to be of [Rare] or [Uncommon] classification.|
|Analysis in progress. I am attempting to capture their existential signatures as they form...|
The sky above the First Folds, a swirling, chaotic canvas of nascent Wheels and forgotten concepts, was torn asunder.
From the blooming Glyphs, the summons began.
From one, a mountain erupted into existence!
A mountain!
Not a projection, but a real, physical thing of impossible scale, its peak scraping against the very firmament of the Fold.
It was a titan of granite and primordial rage, and its single, baleful eye, a molten core of pure, elemental fury, fixed on the approaching legion of Justiciars.
Then, it fell!
BOOOM!
From another, an ancient, colossal tree, its bark the color of polished obsidian, its leaves a storm of razor-sharp, silver blades, burst into being.
It did not attack with fire or light, but with a wave of pure, conceptual silence, a sound-dampening field that sought to erase the very war cries of their enemies!
A third summoned a glacier, a moving continent of absolute-zero ice that was not just cold, but was the very concept of stillness given form.
A fourth birthed a swarm of a billion crystalline locusts, each one a tiny, buzzing engine of consumption.
They came, a pageant of primordial horrors, a menagerie of weaponized concepts!
It was glorious!
It was magisterial!
A skeletal mammoth wreathed in temporal frost, its every step a wave of aging.
A vortex of pure, spatial distortion that sought to fold the Justiciars in on themselves. A single, colossal, golden gavel that descended with the weight of an absolute, unappealable verdict!
The fifteen Astral Arcana Glyphs unleashed their power, a tidal wave of destruction that would have washed away entire Folds.
Before this impossible onslaught, Valkyrie Anastasia's confident, playful smile instantly vanished, replaced by a mask of pure, incandescent rage.
"You fuckers!" she bellowed, her voice a shriek of pure, unadulterated fury.
In the next instant, the thousands of Justiciars behind her moved as one. They did not raise shields; they became the shield.

Their pristine white armor flared with a light so bright it was a physical presence. They interlocked, their forms a perfect, seamless wall of absolute, unyielding Purity. It was a fortress of will, a bastion of unified, technological might!
The fifteen attacks crashed against it.
BOOM!

The mountain shattered. The glacial mammoth dissolved into a cloud of temporal dust. The gavel of judgment was met, and for a single, terrible moment, held. The wall of Justiciars groaned, the light of their unified defense flickering, but it did not break.
They withstood it all, a silent, defiant testament to their own, terrible power.

But... the cost was immense. As the last of the astral attacks faded, as the summoned creatures and concepts dissolved back into the nothing from which they came, a horrifying, mechanical shudder ran through the ranks of the Justiciars.

Nearly half of them began to spasm, their white armor flickering with a chaotic, unstable light. They had used an unfathomable amount of their own internal energy, of their Everythings- a desperate, all-or-nothing defense that had left them on the brink of systemic collapse.
Half of those who had stepped up...were put out of service!
The first clash was over.
And the Elder Early Creatures of Aethelgard, with their ancient, terrible magic, had taken the lead.
Noah watched, his mind a silent quintessential engine of analysis. The Astral Arcana Glyphs were powerful, yes. But they had a cooldown. A limitation.
And yet, if these Elder Early Creatures held dozens, hundreds of such cards in their arsenal, did that limitation truly matter? Their power was genuine. Terrible. And very, very real!
|Master, I was able to capture and analyze the full existential signatures of three of the [Rare] Arcana used in the initial assault.|
|Their power is... considerable. And their mechanics are unique. This is a system of profound strategic potential.|

|School: Elemental|
|Rarity: Rare|

|Description: 'The earth itself is a patient, but unforgiving, judge.' This Arcana summons a Primordial Earth Titan, a creature of living stone and molten fury, from the very bedrock of the Fold. The Titan hurls a single, mountain-sized projectile at a designated area.|
|Cost: 15,500 Units of [Elemental] Everythings, 15,000 Units of [Basic] Everythings.|
|Requirements to Cast: 950 Quadrillion Complexity.|
|Effect: Deals 1,800 Quadrillion in area-of-effect Complexity-based damage. The impact zone is permanently altered, becoming a region of [Unstable Gravity] for 24 hours.|
|Cooldown: 1 Hour.|
|Astral Arcana Glyph|
|Name: The Silent Forest|
|School: Concept|
|Rarity: Rare|

|Description: 'The loudest scream is the one that is never heard.' This Arcana does not summon a creature, but a concept. It manifests an Obsidian World Tree whose presence absorbs and negates all sound, communication, and conceptual 'noise' within its vast radius.|
|Cost: 15,000 Units of [Concept] Everythings, 5,000 Units of [Basic] Everythings.|
|Requirements to Cast: 900 Quadrillion Purity.|

|Effect: All enemies within a dozen Fold light-year radius are afflicted with [Conceptual Muting] for 5 minutes. All abilities with a verbal or communicative component fail to cast. All psionic and mental links are severed. A perfect tool for disrupting a coordinated force.|
|Cooldown: 45 Minutes.|
|Astral Arcana Glyph|
|Name: Chronos's Bargain|
|School: Temporal|
|Rarity: Rare|

|Description: 'I will give you a moment, but the price is a lifetime.' This Arcana summons a Temporal Wraith, a specter of woven time and regret. The Wraith offers a single target a terrible choice: accept a blessing or a curse.|
|Cost: 15,000 Units of [Temporal] Everythings, 1 Unit of [Choice] Everything.|
|Requirements to Cast: 1000 Quadrillion Complexity & Purity.|
|Effect (Blessing): Target ally gains [Temporal Haste]. Their personal timeline is accelerated by 10,000% for 10 seconds. They experience 1000 seconds of existence in a single real-time second.|
|Effect (Curse): Target enemy is afflicted with [Temporal Rot]. Their existence is aged by 10,000 Trillion years in a single instant.|
|Cooldown: 1 Hour.|
Noah nodded as he saw them, his mind already dissecting, analyzing, and calculating the possibilities.
But before he could even begin to truly grasp the strategic depth of this new system, the skies above Aethelgard lit up once more.
The Elder Early Creatures had had their turn. Now, it was time for the youth!
The Juvenile Early Creatures, their forms blazing with a fierce, untamed power, moved to the forefront.
Their own Living Astral Codexes shone, and from them, a new, even more numerous of a storm was unleashed!
HUUM!
Hundreds of Common Astral Arcana Glyphs filled the skies, a blizzard of shimmering, conceptual cards.
It was an avalanche of pure, unadulterated power, a torrent of Early Existential Authority and Early Living Existential Authorities that erupted across the entire region.
The very air was thick with the light of a thousand different summons, a thousand different spells, a thousand different endings all converging on the now-vulnerable forces of the Early Laboratories!
Oh!
Noah's eyes gazed at all of it brightly.
War.
War was also a conversation, was it not? A terrible, brutal, and ultimately, very honest dialogue between two opposing wills.
The first words are often the loudest, the most dramatic...a grand, sweeping statement of intent designed to shock and awe.
A mountain falling from the sky. A forest of silence. A declaration of overwhelming, undeniable power.
But the true, grinding work of war was not in the grand pronouncements. It wS in the relentless, unending stream of smaller, sharper words that followed!
The constant pressure, the endless attrition, the slow, inexorable erosion of the enemy's will to continue the conversation! Through the attacks!
The first blow may be a poem. But the victory is won in the endless, grinding prose that follows.
So just what ridiculously fucking prose was he about to witness here...and who would take the crown at the end of the day?

The attacks raged down towards Valkyrie Anastasia and the remaining Justiciar around her as thousands more appeared, their bodies moving as one to produce countless intricate white chains of Purity that soon formed into a radiant, glorious sea which rose to meet the immensity of Aethelgard.
And soon after, an even grander change bloomed.
A brilliant, crimson glow erupted from the forefront of the Justiciar legion.

Noah was watching absolutely everything as even the slightest changes caught his gaze, and the moment this change came to be...his eyes whipped to very quickly locate exactly where the change started.
Its origin...was Dr. Flamel!
|A Grand Principle has been activated.|
|Analysis: [The Principle of the Crimson Legion] is being initiated by the subject, Dr. Flamel. Its authority is being projected and shared across all allied Justiciar units.|
|Primary Effect: [Legion's Unity] – All Justiciars under the Principle's influence gain a shared pool of Purity and a unified will. Their power is no longer individual, but collective.|
|Secondary Effect: [The Crimson Wings of War] – A temporary, but profound, amplification of all combat parameters.|
BOOM!
The effect was instantaneous and breathtaking. Blazing crimson wings, woven from threads of pure, conceptual fire, bloomed from the back of every single Justiciar!
Their pristine white armor was now tinged with a bloody, warlike light, and their power levels, already staggering, surged to impossible new heights.
The weakest among them now blazed with the light of over 3,000 Quadrillion in Purity, the strongest reaching a terrifying 3,500 Quadrillion!

In this brief, glorious second of empowerment, they did not just defend. They attacked! The white chains of Purity, now infused with the crimson light of the Principle, became whips of absolute judgment!
They lashed out, and the summoned mountains, the silent forests, the temporal mammoths... all of it was torn asunder.
After all each Justiciar now erupted with the power of a genuine Elder Early Creature!
The manifestations of the Astral Arcana were dissected, their very conceptual makeup unraveled and cast into the chaotic winds of the Fold!
And then, with a unified flap of their new, crimson wings, the Justiciars appeared in close proximity... to the wall surrounding Aethelgard in a single instant.
At the Rampart of Aethelgard as they were knocking at the doors!

chapters.title: Chapter 4293: What is The Way? III
paragraphs: The terrifying burst of power, the meticulous and extremely delicate control they had displayed, it all made Noah’s eyes shine!
The Principle that Dr. Flamel wielded... it was a thing of terrible, beautiful efficiency.
In response to this audacious, overwhelming counter-attack, Forgemaster Vulcan and the other Elder Early Creatures simply harrumphed.
A new wave of Astral Arcana Glyphs bloomed above them, but this time, something was different!
From the bodies of the Elder Early Creatures, a new, golden light, the authority of a different Principle, washed over their own forces.
And in the next moment, the sky above the First Folds cracked.
The manifestations of the Astral Arcana Glyphs... they tripled!
Where one Mountain’s Judgment had been summoned, now three identical titans of stone and fury fell from the sky.
Where one Silent Forest had sought to impose its quiet law, now a trinity of them sought to suffocate the very sound of the war.
Chronos’s Bargain, now a trio of temporal wraiths, offered their terrible choices to three different sections of the Justiciar legion at once.
And this applied to all others!
It was a storm of impossible, multiplied power, and it crashed down upon the surging Justiciars with a force that made the very skies crack and boom!
BOOOM!
The massive wall of Aethelgard, the very rampart upon which Noah stood, buzzed with the sheer, overwhelming impact of the collision!
|A second Grand Principle has been exerted.|
|Analysis: I have identified this as [The Principle of Bountiful Repetition]. A terrifyingly efficient offensive tool.|

|Effect: Allows the user to cast a single Astral Arcana and have its effect manifest multiple times. The number of repetitions is dependent on the caster’s own Complexity and the amount of Everythings they are willing to expend.|
|Conclusion: This is at the end of the day, a battle of Principles, Master. A clash of fundamental, reality-altering philosophies.|
HUUM!
As he watched this glorious, terrible dance of power, Noah’s existence buzzed. He entered a sort of trance, his eyes watching everything with a cold, analytical clarity.
It all seemed like a dance.
One side made a move, and then the other made a move that was even more powerful to counter it.
Then, they incorporated their Principles, and the effects and capabilities of both the Living Existential Armors and the Astral Arcana Glyphs became unfathomably grander!
Noah’s eyes kept their tyrannical luminosity.
He had a faint, almost imperceptible smile on his face.
He was a nameless extra, and no one was paying any attention to him. And in that anonymity, he found a profound, almost giddy, sense of freedom.

He was smiling because the more he watched this calamitous battle, the more he saw. He saw the utilization of the Justiciars, the intricate, beautiful power of the Astral Arcana Glyphs, the oppressive, dominating weight of the Haki that was being exerted by every single Early Creature.
And he saw how all of it, every last bit of it, was ultimately being backed by the singular, glorious allure of Principles.
As he watched, a grand epiphany, a precipice of his own power, bloomed in his mind. He whispered, the words for him and him alone.

"All of these different systems of existence are ones that either THE Living Existences formed for Early Creatures, or simply the innate powers of Early Creatures. Whether it be the Astral Arcana Glyphs, Justiciars, Glyphs, or Haki..."
He paused, a universe of possibilities opening before him.
"All of it was made and designed by others."
A new, more profound, and utterly tyrannical thought took root.
He was not just a user of systems. He was a creator. His Way of Existence was not to follow, but to forge.
He did not have to utilize these strict means and systems of existence of others. He could use their skeletons, their backbones, as mere references to make his own, grander system of existence!
HUUM!
He watched the war, at how, no matter what system was being used, all of them were being strengthened by Principles.
The answer was so simple, so elegant, so utterly, beautifully, terrifyingly obvious. He would design his own system!

A system that incorporated the burst potential of the Astral Arcana Glyphs, the sustained power of Haki, the symbiotic growth of a Living Existential Armor... and he would bring it all together under the grand, glorious, and absolute light of his own Principles.
He had already forged his own Principle of Cheating Architect and thr Living Existential Armor.
As for the others...
THE Living Existences gave the methodology of creating more Astral Arcana Glyphs to Gilgamesh? And one could only get that methodology from him? Fuck that.
He would simply forge his own system and make his own Arcana Glyphs!

Whatever they made, he would redesign and incorporate into something even grander. He would put it all and integrate it gloriously under the brilliant allure of Principles. After all, were Principles not the very weavings of Existence?
Noah’s thoughts buzzed brilliantly, and his entire body, even in its suppressed state, began to circulate with a maddened, joyous fervor.
|A moment of Quintessential Epiphany has been achieved.|
|Your Drops of Blood of an Early Creature are multiplying at a tremendous rate as your very being realigns to this new, grand design.|
|Your Towers of Osmont are surging with a new, exponential growth, their light reaching for a new, higher stage.|
|Your Heart pulses with an immensity that it has never felt before. It senses... The Way.|
|Your Way.|
|You have just stepped on the long and arduous, but ultimately, glorious road... leading to Your Way of Existence!|
Oh!
He could sense it.
He felt his endless waves of mana seething like a tumultuous sea that were telling him... guide us, tell us exactly where to go!
He smiled as he felt the fervent glare of his existence that threatened to spill out. Yes, he sensed his pathway, but he did not yet grasp it.
Others had the Way of Hunger.
The Way of Origin.
The Way of Paradox.
There were countless ways out there for him, and there were also none.
The day that he truly stepped and accepted a particular Way of Existence... that would be a grand day indeed!

chapters.title: Chapter 4294 What is The Way? IV
paragraphs: The Way of Existence.
The Way of Life!
Some say the good life is one guided by reason and moral principles, achieved through the pursuit of knowledge and self-improvement.
Others say one must conquer challenges by using reason to control reactions and align with purpose, to accept what cannot be changed and find joy in the present moment!
Accept what cannot be changed.
Still others say the Way to live... was the love of fate.
To love everything that happens in your life, including the pain and adversity, as a necessary part of the whole.

But to truly find one's Way of Life, one's Way of Existence... one had to develop a framework for how you understand the world, then make life choices based on this framework, and then be open to new information and insights!
Well, some say that this was how one could find their Way and perfect it... who knows whether they were right or wrong!
In the Earliest Folds.
That same brilliant Fold Dweller who talked about whether mathematics were discovered or invented found himself staring at the distant skies of his world.
The night was a perfect, profound black, a canvas of absolute nothingness that made the stars burn with a fierce, almost desperate, light.
They were scattered across the void like spilled diamonds on black velvet, distant and cold and beautiful, each one a promise of a world he could only reach out to, but never, ever grasp.
A sigh escaped him, a small cloud of mist in the cool night air. His thoughts were a quiet, insistent hum against the great silence of the cosmos.

"Are we alone?" he whispered to the uncaring stars. "In all this vastness, this glorious, terrifying, and beautiful expanse of existence... am I truly just a solitary voice shouting into an empty hall? It cannot be. The numbers, the probabilities... they all scream that there must be others. There should be countless things out there. Other minds to wonder, other eyes to see, other hands to reach out and try to touch the face of this grand, silent mystery."
He spoke with conviction, a scientist's faith in the elegant, undeniable logic of a universe teeming with possibility!
But as always, like the hundreds of nights before, the night sky retained its calmness.
Nothing changed. The stars did not answer.
He turned, the familiar weight of his own, small existence settling back upon his shoulders, and began to walk back towards the warm, familiar light of his Planetarium.
But the moment he turned around, he jumped back, his heart a frantic, terrified drum in his chest.
Behind him... were three hooded women. He could not see their faces. They were shrouded in a darkness so profound, so absolute, that even when he blinked and squinted, he could not pierce the veil.
They held an air that made him feel stifled, uncomfortable, as if the very laws of physics had taken a step back in their presence.

But he was a brilliant mind, and fear was just another variable to be analyzed. He asked them calmly, his voice a steady, scientific inquiry in the face of the impossible, "Who are you? And what are you doing here?"

Their reply was a thing of impossible, terrible beauty. They spoke in perfect unison, three distinct voices... one high and melodic, one low and resonant, one a dry, academic whisper... all saying the exact same words at the exact same time!
The sound was like honey to the ears, a sweet, seductive melody that promised answers to questions he hadn't even thought to ask.
"We are... THE Weavers."
THE Weavers!
The brilliant Fold Dweller heard this and blinked. Then, with a slow, deliberate motion, he reached into his pocket and took out his phone. He backed away from the women, his thumb already dialing.
"Okay," he said, his voice calm, but with a new, sharp edge of practicality. "Just hold on for a second. I am calling for security."
Yet as he held the phone to his ear, he realized it was dead. Not just powered down, but utterly, conceptually inert.
And even more dreadful, when he looked around, he could not find the familiar trees that had been just near him.
This entire area, his comfortable, predictable patch of the world, was now isolated and dark, with only the vast, silent night sky visible.
A creeping, irrational fear, a feeling he despised, began to rise within him.
"What is this?" he asked, his voice now a little less steady. "Who are you?"

Only now did the three women speak again, their synchronized voices a gentle, almost chiding, question. "Every night you reach out to the stars. Why do you not simply take a step and see them with your own two eyes?"
The brilliant Fold Dweller, now on the back foot but still a scientist at his core, felt a surge of annoyance.

"Number one," he began, his voice a sharp, lecturing tone, "it is impossible to simply 'take a step' and reach the stars. The distances are astronomical. The nearest one is light-years away. And even if I could, number two, do you have any idea what happens to a human body in the vacuum of space? The lack of atmospheric pressure would cause the nitrogen in my blood to form bubbles, a condition known as ebullism. My lungs would rupture. The moisture on my tongue and in my eyes would boil away. I would be flash-frozen and irradiated simultaneously. It would be a very unpleasant, and very final, death."
THE Weavers calmly listened to his detailed, scientific, and utterly correct analysis.

They shook their heads, a slow, synchronized gesture that was more unsettling than any threat. "Have you ever tried to simply take a step to appear in outer space?" they asked, their voices a gentle, persistent prod.
"Have you ever tested whether you could survive in outer space? How do you know you cannot, if you don't try?"

At such questions, the Fold Dweller felt a new wave of annoyance. "What do you mean, how do I know if I don't try? I know exactly what will happen. Science tells me what will happen. The way the world works, the way that nature works, tells me what would happen."
The Way.
The moment he said this, THE Weavers spoke, their unison voice now holding a new, profound weight.

"All of that... is simply what others decided what nature is. You are different. Your Way of Existence is special, unique compared to others. What is known as a fact of reality may not be a fact for you. You could bend it and change it. You could take a step and truly appear all the way in outer space with that single step. You could decide that nature is wrong. That when you are out there in outer space, you could simply survive and breathe what you decide to breathe. That your heart will keep on beating, that your lungs will keep on working. You could simply decide that that was your Way. Your nature. Why don't you... give it a try?"

Why doesn't he give it a try? The brilliant Fold Dweller was utterly tired of these women, these charlatans who seemed to be trying to act like witches or magicians from a forgotten, unenlightened age.
Science was the only truth. Logic was the only path.
So, just to make them go away, to prove the absurdity of their claims, he sighed, a sound of profound, weary condescension.
"Okay," he said. "Here I go. Taking a step. And I will appear in outer space before... oh, the Virgo Star Cluster, how about that?"
With a final, exasperated look at the three hooded figures, the brilliant Fold Dweller took a single step forward.
And...
WAP!
He disappeared in front of the three hooded women!
They looked at each other, and in the deep, impenetrable veils below their faces, they smiled subtly. In eerie synchronicity, they spoke, their voices a quiet, terrible, and absolute verdict.
"Now...one of the core weapons against THE Creature has been put in play..."

sentences.text: The Way of Existence.
The Way of Life!
Some say the good life is one guided by reason and moral principles, achieved through the pursuit of knowledge and self-improvement.
Others say one must conquer challenges by using reason to control reactions and align with purpose, to accept what cannot be changed and find joy in the present moment!
Accept what cannot be changed.
Still others say the Way to live... was the love of fate.
To love everything that happens in your life, including the pain and adversity, as a necessary part of the whole.

But to truly find one's Way of Life, one's Way of Existence... one had to develop a framework for how you understand the world, then make life choices based on this framework, and then be open to new information and insights!
Well, some say that this was how one could find their Way and perfect it... who knows whether they were right or wrong!
In the Earliest Folds.
That same brilliant Fold Dweller who talked about whether mathematics were discovered or invented found himself staring at the distant skies of his world.
The night was a perfect, profound black, a canvas of absolute nothingness that made the stars burn with a fierce, almost desperate, light.
They were scattered across the void like spilled diamonds on black velvet, distant and cold and beautiful, each one a promise of a world he could only reach out to, but never, ever grasp.
A sigh escaped him, a small cloud of mist in the cool night air.
His thoughts were a quiet, insistent hum against the great silence of the cosmos.
"Are we alone?" he whispered to the uncaring stars.
"In all this vastness, this glorious, terrifying, and beautiful expanse of existence... am I truly just a solitary voice shouting into an empty hall?
It cannot be.
The numbers, the probabilities... they all scream that there must be others.
There should be countless things out there.
Other minds to wonder, other eyes to see, other hands to reach out and try to touch the face of this grand, silent mystery."
He spoke with conviction, a scientist's faith in the elegant, undeniable logic of a universe teeming with possibility!
But as always, like the hundreds of nights before, the night sky retained its calmness.
Nothing changed.
The stars did not answer.
He turned, the familiar weight of his own, small existence settling back upon his shoulders, and began to walk back towards the warm, familiar light of his Planetarium.
But the moment he turned around, he jumped back, his heart a frantic, terrified drum in his chest.
Behind him... were three hooded women.
He could not see their faces.
They were shrouded in a darkness so profound, so absolute, that even when he blinked and squinted, he could not pierce the veil.
They held an air that made him feel stifled, uncomfortable, as if the very laws of physics had taken a step back in their presence.
But he was a brilliant mind, and fear was just another variable to be analyzed.
He asked them calmly, his voice a steady, scientific inquiry in the face of the impossible, "Who are you?
And what are you doing here?"
Their reply was a thing of impossible, terrible beauty.
They spoke in perfect unison, three distinct voices... one high and melodic, one low and resonant, one a dry, academic whisper... all saying the exact same words at the exact same time!
The sound was like honey to the ears, a sweet, seductive melody that promised answers to questions he hadn't even thought to ask.
"We are...
THE Weavers."
THE Weavers!
The brilliant Fold Dweller heard this and blinked.
Then, with a slow, deliberate motion, he reached into his pocket and took out his phone.
He backed away from the women, his thumb already dialing.
"Okay," he said, his voice calm, but with a new, sharp edge of practicality.
"Just hold on for a second.
I am calling for security."
Yet as he held the phone to his ear, he realized it was dead.
Not just powered down, but utterly, conceptually inert.
And even more dreadful, when he looked around, he could not find the familiar trees that had been just near him.
This entire area, his comfortable, predictable patch of the world, was now isolated and dark, with only the vast, silent night sky visible.
A creeping, irrational fear, a feeling he despised, began to rise within him.
"What is this?" he asked, his voice now a little less steady.
"Who are you?"
Only now did the three women speak again, their synchronized voices a gentle, almost chiding, question.
"Every night you reach out to the stars.
Why do you not simply take a step and see them with your own two eyes?"
The brilliant Fold Dweller, now on the back foot but still a scientist at his core, felt a surge of annoyance.
"Number one," he began, his voice a sharp, lecturing tone, "it is impossible to simply 'take a step' and reach the stars.
The distances are astronomical.
The nearest one is light-years away.
And even if I could, number two, do you have any idea what happens to a human body in the vacuum of space?
The lack of atmospheric pressure would cause the nitrogen in my blood to form bubbles, a condition known as ebullism.
My lungs would rupture.
The moisture on my tongue and in my eyes would boil away.
I would be flash-frozen and irradiated simultaneously.
It would be a very unpleasant, and very final, death."
THE Weavers calmly listened to his detailed, scientific, and utterly correct analysis.
They shook their heads, a slow, synchronized gesture that was more unsettling than any threat.
"Have you ever tried to simply take a step to appear in outer space?" they asked, their voices a gentle, persistent prod.
"Have you ever tested whether you could survive in outer space?
How do you know you cannot, if you don't try?"
At such questions, the Fold Dweller felt a new wave of annoyance.
"What do you mean, how do I know if I don't try?
I know exactly what will happen.
Science tells me what will happen.
The way the world works, the way that nature works, tells me what would happen."
The Way.
The moment he said this, THE Weavers spoke, their unison voice now holding a new, profound weight.
"All of that... is simply what others decided what nature is.
You are different.
Your Way of Existence is special, unique compared to others.
What is known as a fact of reality may not be a fact for you.
You could bend it and change it.
You could take a step and truly appear all the way in outer space with that single step.
You could decide that nature is wrong.
That when you are out there in outer space, you could simply survive and breathe what you decide to breathe.
That your heart will keep on beating, that your lungs will keep on working.
You could simply decide that that was your Way.
Your nature.
Why don't you... give it a try?"
Why doesn't he give it a try?
The brilliant Fold Dweller was utterly tired of these women, these charlatans who seemed to be trying to act like witches or magicians from a forgotten, unenlightened age.
Science was the only truth.
Logic was the only path.
So, just to make them go away, to prove the absurdity of their claims, he sighed, a sound of profound, weary condescension.
"Okay," he said.
"Here I go.
Taking a step.
And I will appear in outer space before... oh, the Virgo Star Cluster, how about that?"
With a final, exasperated look at the three hooded figures, the brilliant Fold Dweller took a single step forward.
And...
WAP!
He disappeared in front of the three hooded women!
They looked at each other, and in the deep, impenetrable veils below their faces, they smiled subtly.
In eerie synchronicity, they spoke, their voices a quiet, terrible, and absolute verdict.
"Now...one of the core weapons against THE Creature has been put in play..."

chapters.title: Chapter 4295 What is The Way? V
paragraphs: THE Weavers had uttered dreadful words.
As for the Fold Dweller... his eyes opened wide in absolute, soul-shattering shock.
In the next moment, he found that the distant stars he had always been staring at... he was now observing them right in front of his eyes, as if he could simply reach out and touch them.
He was utterly, completely frightened!
When he opened his mouth to scream, no sound came out. He flailed around, a puppet in a stringless void, feeling the strange, terrifying absence of gravity.
In his terror, his mind, still a brilliant, analytical engine even in the face of its own annihilation, remembered the words of the three hooded women.
Simply ignore nature.
Do things your Way. If your Way was to be able to survive in space, then you could survive in space!
He thought this, his mind a desperate, pleading mantra against the crushing, absolute truth of the void.
Because he knew, with a certainty that was its own form of terror, that if he did not think so, he may just crumble and perish in the next moment.
And...
He breathed.
He opened his eyes. In front of him, the distant sun, Procyon, shone with a brilliant, beautiful light, and he was not burned to oblivion.
He was in space. He was alive.
He was breathing. Simply because he had chosen to defy nature, to defy the Way of Existence that had always been established.
He had chosen his Way.
He was an entity that had not even an ounce of mana or authority coursing across his body, and yet, here he was, floating in the silent, terrible beauty of the cosmos, having found his Way!
But he... was an anomaly!
It could almost be said with certainty that...nobody else could replicate what he did!
But that was his Way.
And his Way would lead to unfathomable grandeur!
In the same Earliest Folds.
At a different point in time.
Aethelgard.
BOOM!
Noah watched an unfolding war with a sense of peace, his gaze now that of a scavenger, a predator circling a feast of giants.
He looked for the scraps, for the casualties, for the glorious, terrible loot that the chaos of battle would inevitably produce!
And The Dead had begun to appear.
Well, not The Dead in the way his current Era understood them, not the self-resurrecting horrors that defied the very concept of an ending. No, these were simply corpses.
Grand, magnificent, and unbelievably valuable corpses of Early Creatures caught in the crossfire of this terrible, beautiful war.

Occasionally, a Justiciar, a pristine white scion of death, would break through the lines of Aethelgard's defense and decimate a Young Early Creature or a Juvenile Early Creature, their bodies shattering into a million pieces of crystallized potential.
And then, in the next instant, an Elder Early Creature, a titan of bronze and fury, would descend and unmake the Justiciar in a single, retaliatory blow.
Forgemaster Vulcan and the others, their forms wreathed in the light of their own, terrible Principles, began to shred apart the Justiciar legion.
Their pristine white armor, once a symbol of unyielding Purity, now became canvases for the brutal, beautiful art of their destruction!
Some fell to the brilliant, verdant earth. Others crashed onto the Rampart itself, their broken forms a testament to the fact that even the most perfect weapon can be broken!
HUUM!
Noah watched it all, his eyes shining with an ever-grander brilliance.
Because this was the phase of the war he had been waiting for. The messy part. And he wathcdd it all with glory as the utilization of the many different Systems of Existence was a grand form of Loot.
In any war, there came a time when the elegant, strategic dance of the opening moves gave way to a brutal, chaotic brawl.
A time when bodies began to litter the battlefield, when the neat lines of engagement dissolved into a swirling, bloody vortex of mutual annihilation.

Such a thing began to happen now. This was a chance for Noah to reap a harvest of unprecedented proportions. But at the same time, due to the eyes that were potentially gazing at this battle, he had to ask himself... did the risks truly outweigh the benefits?

The more time he spent here, the more moves he made from a nameless background character to something more... all of it opened up a pathway for a mere gaze of an existence from a Higher Scale of Existence to land upon him.
And after that... was collapse.
He breathed out, a slow, deliberate exhalation in the heart of the storm, and he made a choice.
BOOM!
In the next moment, an Astral Arcana Glyph, a stray shot from the ongoing celestial artillery duel, smashed down onto the Rampart itself.

It was a Mountain's Judgment, and its impact was a thing of terrible, beautiful finality. It was not aimed at him, but its purpose was the same: to decimate a group of Justiciars that had landed on the wall!
The deep impact was enough to cause an explosion that threw back multiple entities, their forms, both living and forged, sent hurtling through the air like discarded toys.
In this explosion, a nameless character saw his chance.
He saw the pieces of Justiciars and the shattered remains of Early Creatures being flung in different directions, and with a single, decisive leap, he joined the dispersal!
He was a leaf in a hurricane, a single, insignificant mote of dust in a storm of collapsing stars.
His Innate Omnichalcum Aura Field buzzed as it collected the vibrant Kinetic energy!
He moved past the Rampart and towards the vibrant, primordial earth outside of Aethelgard.
BOOM!
He crashed to the ground, the impact cushioned by the borrowed power that still coursed through his veins!
He...was not the only one.
Nearby, a Juvenile Early Creature, a being of 900 Quadrillion in Complexity and Purity, was locked in a desperate, final struggle with a Justiciar.
The armor's chest was caved in, its pristine white surface now a spiderweb of cracks, its internal systems spasming and collapsing. It was on the brink of its own, final end!
Neither of these two titans, locked in their death-dance, saw the nameless background character who had landed near them, a silent, unseen observer in this grand, terrible play!

chapters.title: Chapter 4296 What is The Way? VI
paragraphs: The Justiciar, even as its existence unraveled, was still the more powerful of the two!
It radiated a final, desperate burst of its authority. A brilliant white light of pure, unadulterated Purity erupted upwards, smashing into the body of the Juvenile Early Creature.
And shockingly, the being was split in half!
BOOM!
And yet, even as its existence collapsed, the Juvenile Early Creature was undeterred.
A faint, golden Grimoire, a Living Astral Codex, shone at its side.
With a final, maddened roar of defiance, it unleashed its last spell.
An Astral Arcana Glyph, a card depicting a single, weeping eye, bloomed in the air.
From it, a beam of pure, conceptual sorrow shot forth. It was not an attack of fire or force, but of pure, weaponized grief!
The Living Existential Authority of Emotive buzzed!
It struck the already-decimated Justiciar, and the armor, which had withstood mountains and glaciers, simply... gave up.
Its light flickered and died. Its systems ceased. And then, as if in a final, spiteful act of mimicry, it too split in half!
BOOM!
Both halves of both beings hit the ground at the same time.
A cloud of primordial dust and dissipated authority rose into the air!
It was one of the more common scenes in a war... mutual destruction, born from a hatred that had bloomed in the heart of the conflict.
Nearby, Noah, who had remained a nameless character this entire time, moved forward.
A small risk was taken.
A small, almost imperceptible burst of his Mana, a whisper of his true, boundless power, spread over the two decimated corpses. And in the next instant, they were gone!
When the dust settled, a Juvenile Early Creature, its form wreathed in the light of its own, terrible power, appeared above the crater.
It looked around, a flicker of confusion in its ancient, starlit eyes. It had heard a roar of defiance, had sensed a final, desperate clash of power.
But now, there was only the caved-in, brilliant earth and nothing else. It tilted its head, a silent question in the quiet aftermath. But it did not have long to ponder.
OOOH!
In the next moment, a Justiciar, its crimson wings blazing, shot down from above, and the war continued.
"You robotic fucker!" the Juvenile Early Creature roared, its own power flaring to meet the attack.
But silently, already a few light-years away, a nameless background character was walking away!
Each step was a masterpiece of controlled, quantum movement, his feet painted with the Living Existential Authority of Quantum.
With a single step, he was infinitely far away, a ghost disappearing over the horizon!
He was quietly making his exit from the chaotic and utterly dangerous war of Aethelgard.
He did not wait for Gilgamesh to come out. He did not wait for any of THE Living Existences to reveal themselves.
He did not take the risk of remaining on a battlefield where he knew, with an absolute certainty, that THE Living Concept and THE Living Spirit were watching.
He took what he had the chance of obtaining, and he left!
Because sometimes, the single best survival skill in existence was knowing when to take a risk, and when not to.
When to gauge just what could potentially happen based on the risk one took, and whether the rewards were so unimaginably grand to take that risk.

The rewards of the corpses of Young or even Juvenile Early Creatures or Justiciars... did not outweigh the risk of Noah losing his Early Veiled Shore and all those within it by getting the attention of THE Living Existences.
In the past, Gilgamesh had only heard of him and sent his curiosity over, and it had nearly killed him.

He wondered what terrifying potential danger there could be right now, when Gilgamesh inevitably heard of him from Forgemaster Vulcan. A genius Elderborn who could rapidly make Living Existential Armors.
Would he be deemed to have died in battle? Or would Gilgamesh send over another weaving of his Curiosity?
For now, he put all of this in the back of his mind. He felt himself breathing easier as he was now tens of thousands of Fold Light Years away from Aethelgard.
And even then, he continued to move even further. Around him, there were no signs of battles and terrifying eruptions of power.
There was only the vast, stretching, dangerous forests of the First Folds, where he now found himself alone and free to break down the single most profitable loot from that war.
The sensing of his Way.
He now had a few days in the Earliest Folds... to begin designing his own grand system of existence that incorporated everything he had just seen!
He slowed.
Noah arrived in a part of the First Folds that was a breathtaking, frigid wonderland.
Vibrant glacial trees, their bark a shimmering, crystalline blue, rose all around him, their branches heavy with snow that sparkled with the light of a billion captured stars.
Storming, snowy cold winds permeated the air, a constant, gentle blizzard that was a soothing balm on his senses.
He came to a stop in front of a glistening glacial tree that rose up for thousands of miles, its presence a quiet, profound monument to the serene, cold beauty of this place.
The cold here alone could freeze anything below ten Quadrillion, but for Noah, it was... refreshing.
He sat down at the base of the tree, surrounded by the billowing snow and the deep, resonant silence.
He smiled, a genuine, almost peaceful expression, and raised his hand to feel the brilliant, sparkling snow that radiated all around.
It was a unique sensation as he remained in thst peaceful state ever since he sensed his Way.
In his mind, Khor's voice, a warm, ancient echo, resonated.
"I have seen greed kill countless Early Creatures and Living Existences," she said, her tone holding a quiet, profound pride.
"I am proud of you, Outsider, for seeing past your greed in an area filled with unprecedented danger."
Noah only smiled at such words. He nodded lightly, looking at the landscape of stellar, sparkling snow and whiteness all around him.
He gave a small, silent command to RUIN/EDEN.

"Let us begin on the project of... The Way of Existence. Part of it...will be a system of existence that integrates and incorporates everything that we have seen so far under the banner of... Principles."
The command was a quiet, yet absolute, declaration.
A new, grand project had begun. And in response, for the first time in the Earliest Folds, the space beside Noah flickered.
The illusory, holographic form of RUIN/EDEN materialized, her crimson-blue figure a stark, beautiful contrast to the pristine white of the snow.
She smiled, a brilliant, confident expression that was a perfect fusion of Ruination's dark elegance and a system's cool, logical precision.
She bowed towards Noah, her voice a symphony of glorious, terrible possibility!
|I will get started right away, Master.|
As existence began to buzz around him, Noah closed his, snow falling on his body as he thought of what he knew of The Way.
Is it a path to be followed, a map to be read? Or is it something to be forged, a road carved from the raw, untamed wilderness of existence itself?
The philosopher says it is the pursuit of virtue. The mystic says it is the dissolution of the self. The warrior says it is the perfection of the blade. The king says it is the burden of rule.
Each has their answer, each has their Way.
But perhaps, the true Way is not a destination, but a direction!
Not a single, perfect path, but the act of choosing a path at all. It is the conscious, deliberate, and often terrifying, decision to say who you were and what you stood for!
And in the end, it does not matter if the path is one of peace or of war, of creation or of destruction.
Any path, followed with enough conviction, with enough will, with enough of one's very Everything... will eventually lead to a place of unfathomable glory!
"Well...maybe" Noah smiled, opening his eyes.
Maybe!

There was only the vast, stretching, dangerous forests of the First Folds, where he now found himself alone and free to break down the single most profitable loot from that war.
The sensing of his Way.
He now had a few days in the Earliest Folds... to begin designing his own grand system of existence that incorporated everything he had just seen!
He slowed.
Noah arrived in a part of the First Folds that was a breathtaking, frigid wonderland.
Vibrant glacial trees, their bark a shimmering, crystalline blue, rose all around him, their branches heavy with snow that sparkled with the light of a billion captured stars.
Storming, snowy cold winds permeated the air, a constant, gentle blizzard that was a soothing balm on his senses.
He came to a stop in front of a glistening glacial tree that rose up for thousands of miles, its presence a quiet, profound monument to the serene, cold beauty of this place.
The cold here alone could freeze anything below ten Quadrillion, but for Noah, it was... refreshing.
He sat down at the base of the tree, surrounded by the billowing snow and the deep, resonant silence.
He smiled, a genuine, almost peaceful expression, and raised his hand to feel the brilliant, sparkling snow that radiated all around.
It was a unique sensation as he remained in thst peaceful state ever since he sensed his Way.
In his mind, Khor's voice, a warm, ancient echo, resonated.
"I have seen greed kill countless Early Creatures and Living Existences," she said, her tone holding a quiet, profound pride.
"I am proud of you, Outsider, for seeing past your greed in an area filled with unprecedented danger."
Noah only smiled at such words.
He nodded lightly, looking at the landscape of stellar, sparkling snow and whiteness all around him.
He gave a small, silent command to RUIN/EDEN.
"Let us begin on the project of...
The Way of Existence.
Part of it...will be a system of existence that integrates and incorporates everything that we have seen so far under the banner of...
Principles."
The command was a quiet, yet absolute, declaration.
A new, grand project had begun.
And in response, for the first time in the Earliest Folds, the space beside Noah flickered.
The illusory, holographic form of RUIN/EDEN materialized, her crimson-blue figure a stark, beautiful contrast to the pristine white of the snow.
She smiled, a brilliant, confident expression that was a perfect fusion of Ruination's dark elegance and a system's cool, logical precision.
She bowed towards Noah, her voice a symphony of glorious, terrible possibility!
|I will get started right away, Master.|
As existence began to buzz around him, Noah closed his, snow falling on his body as he thought of what he knew of The Way.
Is it a path to be followed, a map to be read?
Or is it something to be forged, a road carved from the raw, untamed wilderness of existence itself?
The philosopher says it is the pursuit of virtue.
The mystic says it is the dissolution of the self.
The warrior says it is the perfection of the blade.
The king says it is the burden of rule.
Each has their answer, each has their Way.
But perhaps, the true Way is not a destination, but a direction!
Not a single, perfect path, but the act of choosing a path at all.
It is the conscious, deliberate, and often terrifying, decision to say who you were and what you stood for!
And in the end, it does not matter if the path is one of peace or of war, of creation or of destruction.
Any path, followed with enough conviction, with enough will, with enough of one's very Everything... will eventually lead to a place of unfathomable glory!
"Well...maybe" Noah smiled, opening his eyes.
Maybe!

chapters.title: Chapter 4297 Anomaly! I
paragraphs: In the region of immense coldness in the Earliest Folds, Noah's figure could be seen walking around as if he were on a stroll.
The sheer capability of anyone to be walking around a dangerous place like the Earliest Folds without a sense of worry or terror was a wonder in itself!
The last time he was here, he was far below even a single quadrillion in complexity and purity, as small animals could have hunted him down and caused him to end his journey early.
All the previous times that he had been in the Earliest Folds, he did not last too long!

As he walked around and felt the warmth of the blistering storm of snow all around... he smiled as he thought that if he had remained in that terrifying battlefield of Aethelgard, he may have just had this journey end abruptly as well.

And yes, it was correct when he said he felt the warmth of the snow all around. Everything here was filled with concentrated Early Existential Authority that he continued to absorb passively into his existence!

Even if the complexity and purity that he absorbed per second was not so immensely significant to cause any grand changes unless he was here for thousands of years, it was a constant, gentle infusion of power, a reminder of the sheer, untamed potential of this ancient, terrible place.
But yes, he, Noah Osmont, was walking around the Earliest Folds without worry! Well, part of the reason that he could do this was because...
|Master, I have completed a preliminary cartographical survey of the immediate Gigaparsec radius.|

|Analysis: The local biome is... stable, for a given value of 'stable' that includes ambient temperatures capable of freezing concepts. Life is sparse, but potent. I have identified 37 distinct lifeforms ranging from a few trillion in complexity to the low quadrillions. Most appear to be non-hostile unless provoked. Emphasis on 'appear.'|

|Threat Assessment: The strongest creature within a significant radius is a territorial herbivore. A Glacial Woolly Rhino, to be precise. Its power is a fluctuating wave of approximately 5 Quadrillion in both Complexity and Purity.|
As the prompt bloomed, the crimson-blue holographic figure of RUIN/EDEN, who was walking silently beside him, waved her hand.
A perfect, three-dimensional projection of the creature appeared.
It was a magnificent, terrible beast, its fur a pristine, shimmering white that seemed to absorb and refract the ambient light.
Its horn was a single, colossal spire of pure, crystalline ice, and its eyes held a deep, ancient, and profoundly grumpy intelligence.
Noah looked over at it as he nodded. "That should be sufficient for lunch," he said, his voice a calm, even tone that held no trace of concern. "How is the progress for our little project so far?"
He continued to enjoy this rare moment of peace and luxury as he asked her about the progress in designing and creating a profound new system of existence that integrated multiple components.
There were systems made by Early Creatures or THE Living Existences, and then there were systems that he had already forged himself like Existential Artifice—the Weavings of Power.
They all had to be seamlessly integrated together!
|Everything is proceeding smoothly, Master.|

|I am currently running diagnostics and theoretical models on over a million potential pathways for your new, unified System of Existence. The objective is to create a methodology that is not just powerful, but is a perfect, quintessential reflection of your own nature. I am eliminating all pathways that do not meet this standard.|

|Addendum: The Living Astral Codex we... 'acquired'... from the corpse of that Juvenile Early Creature has been an invaluable source of data. Its mechanics are crude, but the underlying principles are fascinating. A useful, if somewhat primitive, piece of technology.|
Yes. He had gone through the corpses of the two entities that had undergone mutual destruction.
The entity inside the Living Existential Armor had actually been a Fold Dweller, piloting that glorious monstrosity that held more than one thousand Quadrillion in Purity.
As for the Early Creature... from its remains, he had gotten his hands on a Living Astral Codex that held four Astral Arcana.

Three common ones and one uncommon. They had all been utilized to further understand the system, and RUIN/EDEN had even requested to break down one of the Astral Arcana Glyphs... for the sake of research, of course.
Noah smiled as he continued to walk across the vibrant, snowy lands. Here, he had time. Here, he had peace.
He couldn't freely walk around like this if he were back in his current Era, where he knew things were barreling towards destruction.
He was thinking of the many ways he could go about things as he came to a stop.
He felt a movement, a faint, almost imperceptible stirring in the air before him.
And he saw it. A vibrant blue butterfly.
It was a thing of breathtaking, impossible beauty. Its wings were not of flesh, but of pure, crystalline ice, their surfaces etched with intricate, fractal patterns of frost.

It fluttered through the swirling, snowy winds, not fighting against them, but dancing with them. It landed on a glacial flower, its petals frozen in a state of perpetual, perfect bloom, and with a delicate, almost reverent, touch, it began to drink.
Not nectar, but the very essence of the cold, the pure, untainted authority of this frozen world.
Noah observed it with a sense of profundity.
This creature, in its simple, beautiful, and utterly focused existence, was a perfect expression of its own Way.
|Azure Frostwing|
|Classification: Primordial Glacial Butterfly|

|Analysis: This creature is aware of your presence, Master. However, it exhibits no fear. Its Way of Existence is one of peaceful, focused consumption and propagation. It has correctly assessed that your own Way, at this moment, does not include the pointless annihilation of a being that is not a threat. It is... a very logical butterfly.|

Noah smiled at this observation as he rose up from looking at the butterfly and wondered... should he maybe go around observing different life forms and what their Way of Existence was? Or even possibly...
Noah's eyes shone with a brilliant, almost manic, light.
He looked at the butterfly again, and from his body, a glorious, writhing mass of humanoid tentacles, the form of Ozymandias, appeared.
Part of him was an Inevitability, and he inherently felt The Way of Hunger that Khor had mentioned.
But what if he simply tried to experience other Ways of Existence?

chapters.title: Chapter 4298 Anomaly! II
paragraphs: Whether they were as simple as this butterfly or as grand as a Fold Dweller or a Living Existence or an Early Creature.
At such a thought, Noah smiled.
In the next moment, his body vibrated with authority. His form began to change, to shimmer, to dissolve and reform.
And gradually, he transformed into the same shape as the blue, snowy butterfly.
RUIN/EDEN blinked, her holographic form flickering for a fraction of a second. She looked at her Master, at the perfect, crystalline replica of the Azure Frostwing he had become, and she smiled.
A genuine, almost fond, expression. She then turned back to the complex, swirling data streams of her work.

Noah, in his new, delicate form, flew towards the other butterfly. He landed on the same glacial flower and began to do as it did, to drink the essence of the cold, to experience the world not as a Tyrant, not as The Early Creature, Osmont, but as a simple, beautiful, and utterly focused creature of the frost.
The original butterfly turned its vibrant, multifaceted eyes towards him, and in its gaze, there was a profound, almost comical, sense of bewilderment.
A look that clearly said... Bro, you are a being of Quadrillions of power. Why the hell are you playing around over here right now?
Off to the side, Ozymandias breathed in the snowy environment, devouring everything that came near him.
This part of him took a single step and disappeared, off to further experience...The Way of Hunger.
But in such a manner, Noah began.
He had transformed into another creature for the purpose of understanding and living their Way of Existence.
It may be called imitation, as he didn't completely and truly become a butterfly, but it was a start.
This was how he was spending his time in the Earliest Folds, a moment of profound and utter peace for him.
How exactly were other people faring as the hours passed?
An unknown number of hours later.
Aethelgard.
In the aftermath, there was a profound, terrible silence!
The war for Aethelgard had ended with the quiet, dignified retreat of a force that had tested the walls of a fortress and found them...glorious!

The tens of thousands of Justiciars, their pristine white armor now scarred and broken, had withdrawn, their disciplined silent departure a stark, chilling contrast to the chaotic and vibrant life of the First Folds.
They left behind a scene of breathtaking, terrible carnage.
The Rampart of Aethelgard, once a seamless, golden bastion of impossible beauty, was now a fractured, broken thing in one section!
A massive section of the wall had been torn asunder, a gaping, league-wide wound in the city's defenses.
It was here that the fiercest fighting had taken place, a focal point where the full, overwhelming might of the Justiciar legion had been brought to bear.
And it was here, floating silently before the broken walls, that a new figure had appeared.
He was a king cast in the mold of countless grand Early Creatures!
Gilgamesh, The First Leader!
His form was a perfect, terrible masterpiece of primordial wonder, his golden hair a cascade of starlight, his eyes the color of a dying sun.
He wore a simple, elegant white chiton, yet his very presence was a crown, a declaration of absolute, unyielding dominion!
He gazed out at the battlefield, at the scattered, broken bodies of his own people and his enemies, and his expression was a mask of cold, unreadable contemplation.
The brilliant, verdant earth of the First Folds in the region next to the Rampart was now a graveyard.
The corpses of Early Creatures, their once-glorious forms now shattered and broken, lay scattered amidst the twisted, metallic husks of the Justiciars.
Fold Dwellers and Living Existences who had been caught in the crossfire were strewn across the landscape like fallen leaves, their small, insignificant endings a footnote in a war of titans.
Forgemaster Vulcan stood amidst the devastation, his massive, bronze form a silent monument to the battle that had just been waged.
His starlit eyes, which had witnessed the birth of Folds, now held a deep, ancient weariness.

He looked around, his gaze sweeping over the carnage, and then his expression hardened. He turned to a nearby Juvenile Early Creature, a being of a few hundred Quadrillion whose face was a mask of exhausted relief.
"Where is the Elderborn, Osmont?" Vulcan rumbled, his voice the sound of a mountain demanding an answer.
The Juvenile Early Creature blinked, a flicker of confusion in his eyes. He scratched the back of his head, a gesture of profound, almost comical, uncertainty.
"He... I seem to have forgotten about him amidst the war," he stammered.
Vulcan's eyes blazed with a sudden, terrible fury.
The fuck did he mean he forgot?!
The air around him crackled, the very ground trembling under the weight of his rage.
"You better hope he isn't one of the casualties down below," he roared, his voice a thunderclap that shook the very foundations of the broken wall nearby.
"Go! Look through every single one of them!"
He looked out at the lines of corpses ahead.
Oh!
This was war!

A grand, terrible, and ultimately, very messy affair. It is not the clean, elegant chess match that strategists imagine, but a chaotic, bloody brawl where the best-laid plans are often the first casualty. The aftermath is a landscape of broken things... broken bodies, broken walls, broken certainties.
But in that brokenness, in the quiet, somber aftermath, a new kind of clarity can be found.
For it is only when the noise of battle has faded, when the dust has settled, that one can truly see the cost of victory, the price of survival.
It is in the silence of the graveyard that the true, terrible lessons of war are learned. And it is a lesson that is written not in ink, but in blood.
In a place that was not a place, in a workshop where ideas were not just thought, but forged from the very fabric of conceptual reality, THE Living Concept stood in quiet contemplation!
Before it, on screens of pure, informational light, the recent, cataclysmic battle for Aethelgard played out on a silent, analytical loop.
It watched the glorious, terrible dance of Principles, the brutal efficiency of the Justiciars, the chaotic, beautiful storm of the Astral Arcana, Haki, and Glyphs thst flashed incessantly.
It was in this state of profound, logical immersion that a new presence made itself known.
A wave of contemplative melancholy, tinged with a flicker of something almost like amusement, washed over the space.
THE Living Emotive had arrived.
Halfway through the battle, it had gone above Aethelgard itself to observe!

"Well," its voice was a melody of a thousand different, subtle feelings all singing in perfect, terrible harmony, "that was quite the show, wasn't it? A beautiful, tragic, and ultimately, very messy, display of all the new toys our little existences have been playing with."
