chapters.title: Chapter 4319 Entry! II
paragraphs: On the other side of The Veil.
A massive, oval, white-obsidian vessel floated through the silent, starless void.
It was The Ashen Ark of Judgment, its surface as smooth and as cold as a polished tombstone.
Upon its vast, flat deck, a legion of The Dead stood in perfect, silent formation. There was no chaotic aura, no mindless rage. There was only a profound, chilling sense of Order.
At the forefront stood Tatiana, her dark hair a stark, beautiful contrast to the pale, deathly perfection of her skin.

Around her, other Dead Early Creatures stood as silent sentinels, and behind them, in hundreds of perfect rows, were Dead Existential Armors, their obsidian-black forms radiating a silent, contained power!
The air was thick with a regality that was both beautiful and utterly terrifying.
The Ashen Ark approached a Tear of The Veil, a jagged, weeping wound in the fabric of their reality.
The Early Creatures around Tatiana watched it with calm, ancient eyes, their expressions unreadable masks of power and purpose.
Tatiana stepped forward, her voice echoing out across the silent deck as they began to cross the threshold.
"We are asked to have a purpose," she began, her tone a perfect, commanding cadence that brooked no dissent.

"We are asked to have a singular focus, a driving will that defines our every action. For many, that purpose is a scattered, chaotic thing, a collection of selfish desires and fleeting ambitions. But for us... for us, there is only one purpose. One Order. Our Way is the Way of THE Dead Order."
HUUM!
Her voice grew stronger, more resonant, a creed spoken into the void!

"We adhere to the Doctrines. The First Doctrine: Order is Salvation. All chaos, all the messy, unpredictable weavings of life, are a sickness. We are the cure. The Second Doctrine: All Endings Are Beginnings. We do not bring death; we offer a new, more perfect, more ordered form of existence. The Third Doctrine: The Will of THE Creature is Absolute. All that we do is in service of a design so grand, so profound, that lesser beings cannot even begin to comprehend it."

She paused, letting the weight of her words settle upon her silent, loyal legion. "Existence has unfolded in the way it has as The Fallout is coming. Our purpose is to establish Order before it does, and afterwards. We are to transform the countless Lifeforms in Existence from The Living... to The Dead. Not kill. Transform. Anyone who kills a single lifeform without a transformation occurring will answer directly to me and the other Commanders."
The Ark was now halfway through the Tear, the chaotic, vibrant light of the living Folds bleeding into their silent, monochrome world.

"We are simply an advanced party, sent to get things started. The Forgemaster and the other Lords of the Cryptlands will soon join us to ensure Order as The Veil continues to thin. There will be those who stand in opposition to what we seek to do, as they do not understand. The protocol for such beings is to transform them first and have them understand later. Understood?"
A single, unified roar, a sound that was both a shout and a silent, psychic affirmation, erupted from the legion behind her. "UNDERSTOOD, MA'AM!"
The Ashen Ark of Judgment crossed fully into the new Fold. An Early Creature, his form regal in a pristine white robe, half of his face a bare, gleaming skeletal structure, floated over to Tatiana.
He whistled, a low, appreciative sound. "Nice speech there, Tatiana. I told you the role of a leader was always meant for you."
Tatiana merely scoffed, her gaze remaining cold and fixed on the new reality before them.
"Remain focused, Valerius."

They had arrived. The air here was thick, vibrant, and alive. They were in the Transcendent Elemental Folds, in a region surrounded by bronze, flowing rivers of earthen elements and sands that shone with a stellar brilliance. It was a world of pure, untamed life.
And that life had just noticed them.
In the distance, a group of Living Elementals, their forms blazing with the bronze light of their authority, froze.
They stared at the Ashen Ark, at the few hundred Dead Early Creatures, at the legions of Dead Existential Armors.

A wave of pure, oppressive Haki, the silent, collective will of the arriving legion, washed over them. And in an instant, their lights were snuffed out. They fell from the sky like extinguished stars, their consciousnesses collapsing under a weight they could not even begin to comprehend.
Tatiana gave a light, almost imperceptible nod. Behind her, a Dead Early Creature, his skin a grotesque, beautiful mosaic of decaying flesh and vibrant, living power, flew out.
He moved towards the unconscious Elementals... a paltry force of three Honored and nine Prime Living Existences, their combined complexity a mere whisper against the storm that had just arrived.

The Early Creature came to a stop before the first of the fallen Elementals. He raised a hand, his fingers long and skeletal, and plunged it into the creature's chest. His hand sank in as if through butter.
He did so rapidly in the span of a nanosecond for all the Living Elementals here!
And then, the shocking phenomenon of... The Change began.
On the first Elemental.

A brilliant, obsidian-white light erupted from the point of contact. It was not a destructive light, but a transformative one. It spread across the Elemental's body like a fast-moving frost, its bronze skin turning an ashen, obsidian white. It looked lifeless, and yet, impossibly, the complexity of its existence began to rise!

The process was a terrible, beautiful thing to witness. The vibrant, chaotic energy of the Living Elemental was being... ordered. Refined. Distilled into a new, more potent form of being. The light faded, and the Elemental, now a being of ashen, dead perfection, opened its eyes.

It woke from its state of unconsciousness, and its eyes, once a simple, bronze glow, now shone with a new, grander power and a profound, chilling intelligence. It radiated a power of over one hundred trillion in both Complexity and Purity. A Duke. From a mere Honored, it had become a Duke!
The newly changed Elemental looked at the Dead Early Creature who had transformed it, and it bowed. "Thank you," its voice was a new, resonant thing. "How can I be of service?"

The Dead Early Creature nodded. "Return to your homes," it commanded, its voice a low, rumbling echo. "And grant this Change to others. Do it silently. Make the spread as vast as possible before any conflicts arise."
The new Duke, and the twelve others who had been similarly transformed in a silent, terrifyingly efficient process, bowed as one.
They turned and flew back towards their home, towards... The Heart of Elementals.
Back on the Ark, Tatiana watched this scene with a calm, almost detached, expression. The vessel had now fully entered the Transcendent Elemental Folds.
But in the next second, she frowned. She sniffed the air. Her eyes, which had been as cold and as still as a frozen lake, now showed a flicker of surprise. She sniffed again.
"Can you all smell that?" she asked, her voice a low, puzzled murmur.
The Early Creatures behind her stirred, their own ancient senses reaching out. A collective, silent gasp rippled through their ranks. They could smell it too!

Tatiana's eyes turned sharp, a dangerous, inquisitive light burning in their depths. "I can smell Order," she said, her voice a low, dangerous whisper. "But... Living Order. How could there be Living Order on this side of The Veil?!"
WAA!

They all knew Order was dead. Dead, but still gloriously present, as could be seen through them. But this... this was different. This was a vibrant, living echo of a power that should have been an impossibility.

Tatiana's gaze was a thing of pure, unadulterated focus. She turned to her legion. "You three," she commanded, her voice a sharp, cutting command, "report this back to Forgemaster Vulcan. The rest of you... let us follow the light of Order and see why it is emanating on this side of The Veil... and whether it is true Order, or False Order!"

sentences.text: On the other side of The Veil.
A massive, oval, white-obsidian vessel floated through the silent, starless void.
It was The Ashen Ark of Judgment, its surface as smooth and as cold as a polished tombstone.
Upon its vast, flat deck, a legion of The Dead stood in perfect, silent formation.
There was no chaotic aura, no mindless rage.
There was only a profound, chilling sense of Order.
At the forefront stood Tatiana, her dark hair a stark, beautiful contrast to the pale, deathly perfection of her skin.

Around her, other Dead Early Creatures stood as silent sentinels, and behind them, in hundreds of perfect rows, were Dead Existential Armors, their obsidian-black forms radiating a silent, contained power!
The air was thick with a regality that was both beautiful and utterly terrifying.
The Ashen Ark approached a Tear of The Veil, a jagged, weeping wound in the fabric of their reality.
The Early Creatures around Tatiana watched it with calm, ancient eyes, their expressions unreadable masks of power and purpose.
Tatiana stepped forward, her voice echoing out across the silent deck as they began to cross the threshold.
"We are asked to have a purpose," she began, her tone a perfect, commanding cadence that brooked no dissent.
"We are asked to have a singular focus, a driving will that defines our every action.
For many, that purpose is a scattered, chaotic thing, a collection of selfish desires and fleeting ambitions.
But for us... for us, there is only one purpose.
One Order.
Our Way is the Way of THE Dead Order."
HUUM!
Her voice grew stronger, more resonant, a creed spoken into the void!
"We adhere to the Doctrines.
The First Doctrine: Order is Salvation.
All chaos, all the messy, unpredictable weavings of life, are a sickness.
We are the cure.
The Second Doctrine: All Endings Are Beginnings.
We do not bring death; we offer a new, more perfect, more ordered form of existence.
The Third Doctrine: The Will of THE Creature is Absolute.
All that we do is in service of a design so grand, so profound, that lesser beings cannot even begin to comprehend it."
She paused, letting the weight of her words settle upon her silent, loyal legion.
"Existence has unfolded in the way it has as The Fallout is coming.
Our purpose is to establish Order before it does, and afterwards.
We are to transform the countless Lifeforms in Existence from The Living... to The Dead.
Not kill.
Transform.
Anyone who kills a single lifeform without a transformation occurring will answer directly to me and the other Commanders."
The Ark was now halfway through the Tear, the chaotic, vibrant light of the living Folds bleeding into their silent, monochrome world.
"We are simply an advanced party, sent to get things started.
The Forgemaster and the other Lords of the Cryptlands will soon join us to ensure Order as The Veil continues to thin.
There will be those who stand in opposition to what we seek to do, as they do not understand.
The protocol for such beings is to transform them first and have them understand later.
Understood?"
A single, unified roar, a sound that was both a shout and a silent, psychic affirmation, erupted from the legion behind her.
"UNDERSTOOD, MA'AM!"
The Ashen Ark of Judgment crossed fully into the new Fold.
An Early Creature, his form regal in a pristine white robe, half of his face a bare, gleaming skeletal structure, floated over to Tatiana.
He whistled, a low, appreciative sound.
"Nice speech there, Tatiana.
I told you the role of a leader was always meant for you."
Tatiana merely scoffed, her gaze remaining cold and fixed on the new reality before them.
"Remain focused, Valerius."
They had arrived.
The air here was thick, vibrant, and alive.
They were in the Transcendent Elemental Folds, in a region surrounded by bronze, flowing rivers of earthen elements and sands that shone with a stellar brilliance.
It was a world of pure, untamed life.
And that life had just noticed them.
In the distance, a group of Living Elementals, their forms blazing with the bronze light of their authority, froze.
They stared at the Ashen Ark, at the few hundred Dead Early Creatures, at the legions of Dead Existential Armors.
A wave of pure, oppressive Haki, the silent, collective will of the arriving legion, washed over them.
And in an instant, their lights were snuffed out.
They fell from the sky like extinguished stars, their consciousnesses collapsing under a weight they could not even begin to comprehend.
Tatiana gave a light, almost imperceptible nod.
Behind her, a Dead Early Creature, his skin a grotesque, beautiful mosaic of decaying flesh and vibrant, living power, flew out.
He moved towards the unconscious Elementals... a paltry force of three Honored and nine Prime Living Existences, their combined complexity a mere whisper against the storm that had just arrived.

On the first Elemental.

chapters.title: Chapter 4320 An Exchange! I
paragraphs: Inside the small, world-sized isolated bubble that Schrodinger and Leonore Rureaux were invited in.

They walked upon a radiant stellar blue pathway, a bridge of solidified light that cut through an expanse of breathtaking, cosmic beauty. All around them was the allure of a starlit environment, as if this entire isolated domain was a captured piece of the night sky, a private galaxy where the only destination was a single, glowing point of life at its center: a round garden, pulsing with a gentle, welcoming light.

Leonore Rureaux, her form still frail but her crimson eyes now burning with a cold, clear, and rejuvenated light, gazed at the impossible architecture with a flicker of analytical interest. "Before I even meet him," she said, her voice a low, melodic thing that held the sharp edge of a razor, "I am going to bet ten thousand Everythings of Paradox that he is an Early Creature. Would you take that bet, O Herald?"

Schrodinger smiled, a genuine, almost wistful expression. He shook his head, his bearing a stark, absurd contrast to the celestial grandeur around them. "I will agree with you that he is an Early Creature," he said, his voice a quiet, philosophical murmur. "Though none of that would make sense, but existence is filled with impossibilities. Maybe he is simply another impossibility."

With such a conversation taking place, they arrived at the edge of the garden. In the next moment, a figure appeared before them, a silent, graceful materialization at the garden's entrance. It was Malphas. His obsidian butler's attire seemed to drink the starlight, but woven within its fabric were invisible lines of brilliant blue that pulsed with a quiet, contained power. His eyes, no longer just crimson, now danced with a dangerous, captivating glow of crimson-blue, and the authority he emanated was enough to stifle the very air.

His cold gaze swept over them, a silent, dismissive assessment, before it came to rest on Schrodinger. "Please," he said, his voice a smooth, cultured baritone that was both a polite invitation and an absolute command, "this way."

The garden was a masterpiece of impossible, beautiful life. Radiant sacred herbs, their leaves shimmering with the light of a thousand different authorities, grew in perfect, geometric patterns. Trees, their bark the color of polished moonlight, bore fruits that glowed with a gentle, internal fire. And at the very center, arranged in a perfect circle, were elevated cushions of a shimmering blue-gold material. They surrounded a low table, upon which sat pristine, white-gold plates and cups.

Malphas appeared at the table, and with a graceful wave of his hand, he revealed a somewhat crude-looking bucket. It was forged from the heated sands of the Early Veiled Shore, now cooled into a swirling, opalescent glass. But from this humble vessel, he began to pour... the Sacred Mead of Existence.

Schrodinger and Leonore's eyes widened. They could feel it, the terrifying complexity and potency of the white-gold milky liquid as it filled the cups, its very presence a wave of pure, unadulterated life force that made their own ancient existences hum with a forgotten, primal hunger. As for the plates, Malphas waved his hands again, and they were filled with radiant, boiling sacred waters, in which floated perfect, bite-sized pieces of celestial marine life.
After he finished, he rose like a gloriously efficient butler. "The Master will be here soon," he said. "Please, help yourselves."

With those words, he stepped to the side, his posture one of cold, calm, and absolute stillness. Schrodinger couldn't help but stare, his curiosity a palpable, analytical force. "Who are you?" he asked, his voice a low, intrigued murmur. "You should not be a mere Living Existence or Fold Dweller. And you don't seem like an Early Creature, as I have not seen an Early Creature serve anyone. And yet, I cannot shake the immensity that you are giving off..."

Malphas turned his head, his crimson-blue eyes fixing on Schrodinger with a cold, dismissive light. "I am merely a servant of The Master. Even my name is inconsequential. Again, enjoy the refreshments. The Master will be here soon."

The words made Schrodinger even more intrigued. But beside him, Leonore Rureaux had already picked up a glass. She drank the Sacred Mead of Existence, and her eyes lit up, her entire being buzzing with a unique, vibrant radiance.
And then, he arrived.

A figure manifested just outside the garden, a silent, instantaneous appearance that was not a traversal, but a simple declaration of presence. He floated to one of the radiant, elevated cushions and sat. He was adorned in a simple, blue-gold emperor's robe, his hair now a cascade of extremely radiant blue-gold, as if a thousand oceans of Mana were warring for dominance against the light of a captured sun. His fair, white skin was scintillating, shining as if it were crystalline, and it held within it an unfathomable ocean of power. He was an impossible weapon, an emperor in his prime, yet young, and also ancient with a power that defied all comprehension.
The moment he appeared... Schrodinger and Leonore Rureaux both frowned. They felt it.
Suppression!

The two of them, beings of such profound and terrible power, actually felt a sense of suppression in his presence. Noah looked back at them, and beside him, unseen by either of them, the crimson-blue holographic form of RUIN/EDEN materialized.
|Master, the existential signatures of the two subjects have been ascertained.|
|The subject, Schrodinger, is currently radiating a power of 0.5 Quintillion in both Complexity and Purity.|

|The subject, Leonore Rureaux, is at 0.8 Quintillion. My analysis indicates that this is a degraded state; her potential maximum is likely in excess of 2 Quintillion. It seems her previous imprisonment has left her... gravely injured.|

0.5 Quintillion and 0.8 Quintillion. Noah processed the numbers, a cold, tyrannical calm settling over him. The usage of Quintillion meant these entities had already embarked on, or at least sensed, their Way of Existence. This was the Schrodinger he knew, the Living Paradox. But the other one, the defeated, apathetic Living Concept he had seen in the Early Laboratories... if that being was one and the same, then now was the time to learn, to understand.
He sat, his gaze sweeping over the two of them. He nodded once, a gesture of a king granting an audience. "You were looking for me."

chapters.title: Chapter 4321: An Exchange! II
paragraphs: The silence was a taut, humming thing. Schrodinger looked at Noah, and a brilliant, almost dazzling, smile spread across his face. “I’m going to go out on a limb,” he said, his voice filled with a genuine, almost joyous, wonder, “and simply affirm that you are, in fact, an Early Creature. Which begs me to question... How did a piece of the weapon of THE Living Law not work against you?”
Noah looked at him, and his expression was a perfect, unreadable mask.
He appreciated the nature of a being like this who did not beat around the bush too much!

His voice, when he spoke, was not loud, but it was absolute. It was the voice of a man who did not need to raise his tone to command a room, for the room already belonged to him. “As far as I know, the weapon of THE Living Law works against Early Creatures. I am not an Early Creature. I am The Early Creature, Osmont.”
BOOM!
Simply.
Impossibly.
A very straightforward answer was given.

Schrodinger and Leonore’s eyes sharpened, a new, more profound level of calculation entering their gazes. Noah calmly picked up his own glass of Mead and took a sip, his eyes, burning with a quiet, tyrannical fire, still fixed on Schrodinger.

“Now you...” he began, his voice a low, dangerous hum. “You have been a question in my mind for a little while now. I’ve asked myself again and again, what could that Schrodinger be up to? What’s he doing purposefully accelerating Tears of The Veil? What’s he doing with a corpse of an Early Creature? But now, in the grand scale of things, it doesn’t matter too much. What does matter is my curiosity. As I want to ask... do you remember anything regarding the Early Laboratories? Elderborns?”
BOOM!
The Early Laboratories and Elderborns!

Noah asked such a question simply to see exactly what reaction would bloom from Schrodinger, and he saw it. A flicker of sharp, analytical light in both his eyes and the crimson depths of Leonore’s. It was not him who replied, but the woman who was currently more powerful than him.

“With every word you say,” Leonore began, her voice a low, resonant note that cut through the starlit quiet of the garden, “you make it clear to us that you know a whole lot more than you are letting on. We can skip any back and forth and get right to business then-”
“Oh, Elderborns! That takes me back!”
Schrodinger interjected, his voice a bright, almost nostalgic, chime that shattered her serious tone. Leonore turned to him, her expression a mask of pure, unadulterated annoyance.
He simply smiled, a mischievous, almost childlike, glint in his ancient eyes, and gently tapped her thigh as if to say, let me handle this.
He kept his gaze fixed on Noah. “I know a thing or two about Elderborns,” he said, his voice now a conspiratorial whisper. “Do you know their true origins? Let me tell you a story...”
Leonore rolled her eyes, a gesture of profound, weary exasperation. “Really? Right now?”
Yet, Schrodinger’s gaze did not waver from Noah.
Noah, for his part, simply took another slow, deliberate sip of the Sacred Mead of Existence, his expression a calm, unreadable mask. He was a mountain, and their words were but wind.

“Many believed,” Schrodinger began, his voice taking on the cadence of a master storyteller, “that the Elderborns were simply a glorious accident of existence. Beings blessed with a heavily concentrated measure of THE Creature’s Everythings. The First Leader, Gilgamesh, a being of such unyielding ambition that he sought to unite all Early Creatures under a single banner. Tatiana, a weaver of dreams whose power could shape the very fabric of reality. Each a titan in their own right, their power a testament to a glorious, cosmic lottery.”

He paused, letting the weight of the legend settle. Then, his smile turned sharp, dangerous. “But that... is not the case. The Elderborns did not form naturally. They were not an accident. They were a guided emergence from the hands of THE Living Existences. They were... purposeful designs. Which begs you to wonder, why did THE Living Existences seek to cluster the concentrated Everythings of THE Creature onto a few, specific beings?”
Why?

The air in the garden, once so serene, turned heavy and cold. Noah studied Schrodinger and Leonore, his eyes shining with a brilliant, analytical light. “Elderborns were always seen around THE Living Existences, carrying out their whims,” he said, his voice not a question, but a statement of fact, a piece of a puzzle he was now assembling aloud. “Are you going to tell me that THE Living Existences were grooming them as tools or weapons? For their fun? Or against THE Creature?”
BOOM!

At his words, Schrodinger smiled. “That is a great question. Who can say for sure? One can only be certain if they can track what every Elderborn has done across the Earliest Folds. Well, before they and countless other Early Creatures disappeared, which brings us to the next point... the disappearance of Early Creatures and the implausibility of you being here. I’m going to assume you already know a lot about The Fallout?”

Schrodinger spoke the words with a grand, theatrical flourish. Noah calmly raised his glass of Sacred Mead of Existence and drained the last of the shimmering, white-gold liquid. The cup was empty. In the next instant, Malphas appeared beside him, a silent, graceful specter of perfect servitude, the crude, beautiful bucket in his hand as he refilled the glass without a word.
Noah gave a single, almost imperceptible nod of acknowledgment. “I know a little bit about The Fallout.”
Schrodinger’s smile widened, a flash of genuine, almost manic, delight in his eyes.

As if he sought to one-up him, to always hold the final, most devastating card, he leaned forward, his voice a low, triumphant whisper. “We... know where the entrance to a Shelter that can withstand the Fallout is.”
BOOM!

Noah, for his part, simply took another slow, deliberate sip of the Sacred Mead of Existence, his expression a calm, unreadable mask.
He was a mountain, and their words were but wind.
“Many believed,” Schrodinger began, his voice taking on the cadence of a master storyteller, “that the Elderborns were simply a glorious accident of existence.
Beings blessed with a heavily concentrated measure of THE Creature’s Everythings.
The First Leader, Gilgamesh, a being of such unyielding ambition that he sought to unite all Early Creatures under a single banner.
Tatiana, a weaver of dreams whose power could shape the very fabric of reality.
Each a titan in their own right, their power a testament to a glorious, cosmic lottery.”
He paused, letting the weight of the legend settle.
Then, his smile turned sharp, dangerous.
“But that... is not the case.
The Elderborns did not form naturally.
They were not an accident.
They were a guided emergence from the hands of THE Living Existences.
They were... purposeful designs.
Which begs you to wonder, why did THE Living Existences seek to cluster the concentrated Everythings of THE Creature onto a few, specific beings?”
Why?
The air in the garden, once so serene, turned heavy and cold.
Noah studied Schrodinger and Leonore, his eyes shining with a brilliant, analytical light.
“Elderborns were always seen around THE Living Existences, carrying out their whims,” he said, his voice not a question, but a statement of fact, a piece of a puzzle he was now assembling aloud.
“Are you going to tell me that THE Living Existences were grooming them as tools or weapons?
For their fun?
Or against THE Creature?”
BOOM!
At his words, Schrodinger smiled.
“That is a great question.
Who can say for sure?
One can only be certain if they can track what every Elderborn has done across the Earliest Folds.
Well, before they and countless other Early Creatures disappeared, which brings us to the next point... the disappearance of Early Creatures and the implausibility of you being here.
I’m going to assume you already know a lot about The Fallout?”
Schrodinger spoke the words with a grand, theatrical flourish.
Noah calmly raised his glass of Sacred Mead of Existence and drained the last of the shimmering, white-gold liquid.
The cup was empty.
In the next instant, Malphas appeared beside him, a silent, graceful specter of perfect servitude, the crude, beautiful bucket in his hand as he refilled the glass without a word.
Noah gave a single, almost imperceptible nod of acknowledgment.
“I know a little bit about The Fallout.”
Schrodinger’s smile widened, a flash of genuine, almost manic, delight in his eyes.
As if he sought to one-up him, to always hold the final, most devastating card, he leaned forward, his voice a low, triumphant whisper.
“We... know where the entrance to a Shelter that can withstand the Fallout is.”
BOOM!

chapters.title: Chapter 4322 Do Not Idolize! I
paragraphs: Schrodinger stated that he knew where the entrance to a Shelter that could survive The Fallout was!
At such words, Noah's gaze, which had been a calm, almost leisurely thing, sharpened into a point of absolute, tyrannical focus.

The air in the small, world-sized bubble grew heavy, the starlit environment seeming to hold its breath. Beside him, unseen by the two ancient Paradoxes, the crimson-blue holographic figure of RUIN/EDEN materialized, her voice a cool, clinical whisper in his mind.

|Based on my analysis of his existential signature, Master, the subject 'Schrodinger' genuinely believes his words to be true. He is not bluffing or engaging in theatrical misdirection. Whether the information itself is accurate... is a variable that remains unknown.|
Noah looked at Schrodinger, his expression remained a perfect, unreadable mask.
His voice, when he spoke, was a low, resonant, and utterly imposing thing. "To clarify," he began, each word a carefully placed piece on a board of vast scale, "you know the entrance into THE Loom?"

At his words, Schrodinger and Leonore Rureaux looked at each other once more. Schrodinger then smiled, a brilliant, almost dazzling expression of pure, unadulterated amusement. "Well now," he said, his voice a playful, conspiratorial hum, "I am going to continue with my assumption that you already know a whole lot, similar to us, so I'll keep talking. If ever you are lost, just let me know. So... no. I do not have knowledge of the entry to THE Loom. That is an impossibility. THE Loom will never be open, or even have the possibility of opening... until after The Fallout has taken place. Nothing can go in or out. What I have knowledge of is a subsidiary of THE Loom. A small portion of it where those who designed THE Loom... kept their toys."
BOOM!
Their toys.
"You should have met them already," Schrodinger continued, his smile never wavering. "The Justiciars. The Arbiters."
His expression then shifted. The smile vanished, replaced by a look of cold, callous rage so profound it seemed to make the very starlight around them curdle.

"For the designers of THE Loom," he hissed, his voice a venomous whisper, "it wasn't enough that countless existences would collapse. One designer in particular wanted to continue harvesting from its Way of Existence. Its Way of Emotive. That despicable, shitty, bum clusterfuck of an existence, Emotive, placed behind a protocol where as The Fallout approached, its tools would appear to begin reaping and rousing even more emotions."

"To let all remaining existences know they would perish, and as a form of mercy, some would be collapsed even before The Fallout came, the whole thing displayed until the day of The Fallout. What just happened with Aeternitas Glacies was exactly that. To induce fear. To rouse emotions. Because The Fallout itself is not enough... but for their Way of Existence... they will milk it for even more."
BOOM!

Noah's eyes flashed with a chilling light. Beside him, Malphas's arms trembled slightly, not with fear, but with a deep, resonant fury. He glared towards Schrodinger. "THE Living Emotive experienced negative and positive emotions differently," he stated, his voice a cold, hard blade.
"Their Way of Existence would be even more boundless when it fed on positive emotions. Such a thing would not be put in place by THE Living Emotive. They are not like this!"
Malphas had spoken out, his loyalty a shield against the accusation.
Schrodinger's eyes turned sharp, squinting as he analyzed the butler. "How would you know THE Living Emotive's nature so well?"
Malphas did not reply. He stared at Schrodinger coldly, then turned to Noah and bowed, his form a perfect expression of regret. "I apologize for my outburst, My Lord."
Noah nodded towards him, a silent acknowledgment. "It's okay."
His head turned, his gaze sweeping over the vibrant, beautiful garden around them. He sighed.
The Way of Existence.

He thought of the Ways of Emotive and the other Living Existences. He even wondered about the Way of THE Creature. Did all of them treat the countless lifeforms across Existence as their Civilizations? Was this the reason for the endless, teeming life that permeated the Folds?
"Living Paradoxes and how they live day in and day out... feed The Way of Paradox. The Civilization of Paradox," he mused aloud, his voice a low, contemplative rumble.

"Origin feeds the Way of Origin, Law feeds The Way of Law... and so on and so forth." He turned back to Schrodinger, his gaze a sharp, analytical probe. "Where in this does THE Creature come in? Do you know of The Way of THE Creature?"

At his words, Schrodinger shook his head. "That is inconsequential. His Way does not matter. Because THE Creature abandoned us. He went silent. With his nature, he wouldn't have allowed THE Loom to come to fruition, and yet it did. Why is that? Why did he leave us? Why did he abandon us? WHY?!"
Towards the end of his words, Schrodinger's voice rose to a furious, almost desperate, roar. Leonore Rureaux placed a hand on his shoulder, her touch a calm, steadying anchor in his storm of rage.

"THE Creature did not abandon us," she said, her voice firm, unwavering. "I and others always believed that something happened. Something we do not know. Maybe THE Living Existences did something. There is a lot about history we do not know. There is the Curse overflowing across The Dead that we know THE Creature was involved in. The Veil that THE Creature was involved in. We may be misunderstanding many things here..."
Schrodinger looked at her, his expression weary, his rage giving way to a deep, ancient bitterness. He shook his head.
"The dangers of idolizing a common existence as if any of them were different..." he began, his voice now a low drum.

"Idolizing someone can lead to de-existentialization, where we project a fictional image of perfection onto them, denying their own, flawed existence. When they inevitably fail to live up to this image, it leads to intense disappointment and even bitterness. Heavy, heavy bitterness. It can lead to defending inexcusable actions or ignoring evidence of wrongdoing that are blatantly there."

chapters.title: Chapter 4323 Do Not Idolize! II
paragraphs: "THE Creature was born. THE Creature will die, or is already dead. THE Living Existences can be killed just like you and I. Just look at THE Living Order. Deader than Dead. All of them...They eat. They shit. They hate. They fear. They may be higher on the Scale of Existence than us... but they are still that. Existences. I will never fucking idolize them. Not ever again."
His words were heavy, each one a stone dropped into the silent, contemplative pool of the garden.
Malphas looked down, his own thoughts a swirling vortex of loyalty and doubt.

Noah's eyes, however, shone with a bright, tyrannical light. "THE Creature had his Way of Existence, and we have our own," he declared, his voice a calm, absolute verdict. "Yes, we are no different. Regardless of what happened in the past that we do not know, it is the present and future that matter the most. So... this Shelter. Where is it, and how can the vast lifeforms of all Folds be relocated in it to survive The Fallout?"

At his critical question, Schrodinger fell silent. He picked up his drink, downing the entire cup of Sacred Mead of Existence in a single, decisive gulp. His eyes shone with a new, sharp light as he looked at Noah. "When a Justiciar appears again," he said, his voice a low, conspiratorial whisper, "just follow it back to where it came from. Track it. Let it lead you to its base, and it will be a Shelter connected to THE Loom. A tiny little subsidiary. A Garden of Hope. A line of salvation. Reach it, and one may just survive The Fallout."
A heavy silence settled over the garden.
|Master, the new information has been analyzed.|

|The subject 'Schrodinger' is proposing a high-risk, high-reward infiltration mission. The 'Garden of Hope' is likely a forward operating base or a manufacturing facility holding the Justiciars and Arbiters.|

|Feasibility: If such a location exists, and if it is indeed a 'subsidiary' of THE Loom, it may possess a degree of the same protective qualities. It is a viable, if exceedingly dangerous, path. There is no harm in seeing if this is actually true.|
Noah looked at Schrodinger calmly, the two of them locked in a silent, analytical gaze. Finally, Schrodinger spoke again.

"That is one of my goals, anyway. Even if my methods are questioned. Even if some lives are lost. All life will be extinguished in the near future if this solution, or another, is not attained. Since you seem to have enacted your own Way, you have your own drive to survive, and you might even have the mindset of wanting to save those in your Way of Existence. If your existence can cause this body of mine here to feel a sense of suppression, your power could tip the scales if need be. I partly came here to say this, to make sure that you would not be a force of interference in my plans. If we are all going towards the same thing, even better. There is no harm in having an Early Creature with unknown origins bearing the grunt of the weight of Existence. After all... why should I be alone in suffering?"
Why should he be alone in suffering? The words were a quiet, terrible confession, a glimpse into the profound, ancient loneliness of the being before him.
Schrodinger believed himself to be carrying the weight of existence on his shoulders, a self-appointed, and perhaps, self-deluded, savior.

Noah shook his head internally. In existence, one could believe they were a chosen one, a herald, a bringer of apocalypse. But what mattered in the end... was power. Power would ultimately decide what role one played.
He had come across many who thought themselves saviors, and yet they had the highest body count of those they killed.
He did not even have to look far as when he looked at himself...oh!
As Noah was thinking this, his gaze, and the gazes of Schrodinger and Leonore, snapped outwards. Their perception pierced through the blue-gold barrier of their isolated domain, to the chaos beyond.
Behind the teeming, anxious crowds of Living Existences, a massive, flat vessel had appeared, a silent, obsidian white omen in the swirling void.

And on it... were entities so terrifying that their mere Haki caused the nearby Prime, Honored, and Royal Living Existences to lose consciousness, their forms slumping in the void like puppets with their strings cut.
Oh!
Noah's eyes focused, his perception, now a thing of wonder, dissecting the new arrivals.
He saw...Early Creatures!
Dead ones!
And at the forefront, one who shone with tremendous radiance.

He saw... Tatiana, a queen of ordered death, her complexity a staggering 4 Quintillion. He saw the regal, half-skeletal Valerius, his power a calm, terrible 3.5 Quintillion. He saw the others, a legion of The Prime Dead, their power a silent, crushing wave!
|Alert: High-threat entities have arrived.|
|Source: The Folds of The Dead.|
|Primary Signatures:|
| - [Tatiana – The Ashen Dreaming Queen] – 4.1 Quintillion Complexity.|
| - [Valerius – The Silent Regent] – 3.5 Quintillion Complexity.|
| - [Legion of the Prime Dead] – Average Complexity: 2.5 Quintillion.|
Oh!
Beside him, Leonore's voice was a low, dangerous hiss towards Schrodinger.
"Now might be a good time for you to awaken a stronger body. Otherwise, we all may just be fucked."
The Prime Dead had arrived. But as Noah watched, a final, chilling detail registered in his perception, a detail that was confirmed by a final, terrible prompt from RUIN/EDEN.

The gazes of the newly arrived legion, their collective, silent will, was not focused on the assembled forces of the Living, nor on the curious Paradoxes, nor on the enraged Origins. Their attention was fixed, with a profound, almost religious, focus, on the blue-gold fortress of the Infiniverse.
And their bodies, their very auras, were surrounded by a brilliant, pristine, and utterly familiar white light.
|Analysis of The Prime Dead legion is complete. A significant and unexpected anomaly has been detected.|
|Their authority is not just that of The Dead. It is... intertwined with the authority of Order.|
Order.
Oh, Order!

chapters.title: Chapter 4324 Sheer Depravity! I
paragraphs: The area surrounding The Infiniverse became unfathomably silent. Over ninety percent of The Living Existences that had gathered, beings who could command the very fabric of reality, slumped down listlessly.
Their consciousnesses were entirely turned off, snuffed out like candle flames in a hurricane by the mere proximity of the terrifying existences that had arrived!

And yet, like a grand and terrifying sea, these waves of power and suppression that were culminating in Haki actually stopped short, parting like water before a sacred mountain as they neared the blue-gold Aegis of The Infiniverse.
Inside the small, world-sized isolated bubble, Noah stood, his gaze turning from the chaotic, beautiful garden to the scene outside. His eyes were cold, calculating, and utterly, profoundly, calm.
|Master, I am detecting a subtle, yet significant, anomaly in the existential signatures of the newly arrived Prime Dead.|
|Analysis: They are exhibiting... hesitation.|
Hesitation?

Why would such powerful beings hesitate? Their gazes were fixed on his home with an intensity that was almost religious, and their very existence swam with a potent, undeniable allure of Order. Noah could put two and two together. The reason for their hesitation... he did not like the direction his thoughts were taking him.

"The appearance of the Prime Dead is much faster than anticipated," Schrodinger's voice was a low, analytical murmur beside him. "Reinforcements will arrive here soon, but for the most part, all existences here are on their own."

At his words, Noah's eyes flashed brightly. His gaze focused on the figure of the Dead Early Creature, Tatiana. She was floating from the vessel, her hand raised in a gesture that was both a command and a reassurance to her legion. She was moving, shockingly, towards The Infiniverse.

She paid no attention to the dazed, terrified Living Existences. Her focus was singular. She drew closer, and the blue-gold glow of the Aegis reflected on her pale, beautiful, and utterly dead features. And then, she stopped.
Noah watched this being, this queen of a dead empire, and his thoughts were a silent, rapid-fire exchange with his new System. 'RUIN/EDEN. The network of Resplendent Citadels is active, yes?'

|Confirmed, Master. The Civilization Network is online and operating at peak efficiency. All 159 Citadels are linked, their collective power forming a defensive matrix capable of withstanding an attack three times the capacity of your own current Complexity and Purity.|
|Analysis: Sufficient for a protracted defensive engagement against the current threat, but a direct, focused assault from their combined might would be... problematic.|
It may be enough, but the situation was still perilous. And yet, the Prime Dead did not attack. As Noah watched, Tatiana... opened her mouth to speak.
Her voice was a thing of impossible, terrible beauty. It was not a shout, but a clear, resonant pronouncement that carried across the void with the weight of an unshakeable, absolute truth.

"I am Tatiana, the Ashen Dream Queen, First Blade of the Cryptlands of Nagash-Prax. I, and all those you see before you, are followers of THE Creature. We are followers of Order. We revere Order, and we live by its Doctrines. We had altered our course to come here directly because we sensed an allure, a beacon of Order so pure, so potent, that it could not be ignored. And now, having come close, I can affirm that what emanates from within this sanctuary... it is the truest type of Order. Living Order. It is for this reason, and this reason alone, that I show the respect that I currently am."

In the Early Veiled Shore, Noah's other body gently touched Sigrid's shoulder. She came out of her deep, power-infusing cultivation, her form now pulsing with waves of pure, white-gold mana and Order.
She blinked, and as Noah directed her gaze to the scene unfolding outside the Infiniverse, her eyes widened.

Outside, Tatiana continued, her voice a calm, commanding current. "I realize how our appearance here, especially our current state of existence, may seem threatening. It may even cause misconceptions. I wish to clear that up first, before anything else. I know that within this isolated, protective domain, lies a budding Living Order. And it is to you that I speak now, and to nobody else."

Oh!

sentences.text: The area surrounding The Infiniverse became unfathomably silent.
Over ninety percent of The Living Existences that had gathered, beings who could command the very fabric of reality, slumped down listlessly.
Their consciousnesses were entirely turned off, snuffed out like candle flames in a hurricane by the mere proximity of the terrifying existences that had arrived!

And yet, like a grand and terrifying sea, these waves of power and suppression that were culminating in Haki actually stopped short, parting like water before a sacred mountain as they neared the blue-gold Aegis of The Infiniverse.
Inside the small, world-sized isolated bubble, Noah stood, his gaze turning from the chaotic, beautiful garden to the scene outside.
His eyes were cold, calculating, and utterly, profoundly, calm.
|Master, I am detecting a subtle, yet significant, anomaly in the existential signatures of the newly arrived Prime Dead.|

Hesitation?
Why would such powerful beings hesitate?
Their gazes were fixed on his home with an intensity that was almost religious, and their very existence swam with a potent, undeniable allure of Order.
Noah could put two and two together.
The reason for their hesitation... he did not like the direction his thoughts were taking him.
"The appearance of the Prime Dead is much faster than anticipated," Schrodinger's voice was a low, analytical murmur beside him.

chapters.title: Chapter 4325 Sheer Depravity! II
paragraphs: "We chose to stand with THE Creature and find another way. What you see before you is that way. I, and all those behind me, and countless others on the other side of The Veil, all chose to fight against the abomination that is THE Loom."

"The reason for our coming through at this very moment was to lay out the path of survival for the countless masses, as THE Loom prepares to unleash its horrors upon all of existence. I had wished to tell you all of this because we also follow Order... on the other side of The Veil. Order helped us establish who we are today and fight against the tyranny of THE Living Existences against THE Creature. For there to be a piece of THE Living Order in this domain... is not by chance."
Her words were heavy!
So, so heavy!

"And so, after explaining all of this, I hereby invite THE Living Order within to come back with me to the other side of The Veil. Your mere existence... may very well change a tremendous amount of things. With you and the radiant Order that is on the other side of The Veil, the possibilities for existence and its survival against the abomination that is THE Loom... are tremendously altered. Once more... I hereby invite the Young Living Order to come with me to the other side of The Veil."
BOOM!
The invitation was a thing of impossible, terrible weight.
Noah's eyes shone with a terrifying, brilliant light. Schrodinger and Leonore, in their isolated bubble, turned to him, their gazes stern and questioning.
|Master, the information provided by the subject 'Tatiana' is a paradigm-shifting event.|
|Primary Revelations:|
| - [The Fallout] is not a natural event, but a man-made (or rather, Existence-made) one.|
| - [THE Loom] is not a passive sanctuary, but an active, predatory weapon.|
| - A significant faction, aligned with [THE Creature], exists on the other side of The Veil. Their objective is to oppose THE Loom.|
|Strategic Re-evaluation:|
| - The solution of [Halting the Catalyst] is now... significantly more complex. The catalyst is not a single entity, but a coalition of Level One Scale existences.|
| - The solution of [Breaching THE Loom] is now re-contextualized.|
| - The solution of [The First Farmer] remains a viable, if now more urgent, path for a potential third faction and alliance.|

Noah processed the information, his mind a silent storm of calculation. He opened his mouth, and his voice, a calm, resonant, and utterly absolute thing, boomed out from the isolated domain, reaching Tatiana and all those in the surrounding void.
"You have mentioned Order multiple times on the other side of The Veil... just who is embodying Order on the other side of The Veil?"
His voice echoed out.

Tatiana frowned. She did not like that someone other than the Living Order had replied to her. But she answered, her voice as calm and as cold as a tombstone. "On the other side of The Veil, the only Order that has been present and aiding THE Creature has been THE Dead Order."
BOOM!
The Dead Order. One of THE Living Existences... on the side of The Dead.

In the Early Veiled Shore, Sigrid fell to her knees, the revelation a physical blow. But Noah remained calm. His voice boomed out again. "You mentioned THE Living Order from here coming with you to the other side of The Veil... THE Living Order on this side is merely a resurgence, unable to make any grand changes in existence. How exactly would their crossing over change anything in the vast weavings of what is unfolding?"
Tatiana's frown deepened. "I would very much like to be discussing all of this with THE Living Order, and not a bystander."

Noah's eyes flashed with a cold light. "Whether you stand to have any discussion with THE Living Order or not is dependent on whether you answer this question. What exactly would THE Living Order be doing if she crosses to the other side of The Veil?"
The air grew cold. A silent, terrible wave of power pulsed from Tatiana.

But she held it in check. "Out of respect to the Order that we follow, I will answer. THE Living Order coming to the other side of The Veil would mean that THE Dead Order and THE Living Order can come and join together in a profound and unfathomable union that may just be the grandest answer to THE Loom and the abomination of actions that were taken to enact it."
Noah's eyes flashed coldly.

|Master, the probability of a true 'union' is 0.01%. The probability of a complete and total assimilation of the lesser, resurgent Order by the established, primordial Dead Order is 99.99%. She is asking for a sacrifice.|
In the deafening silence that followed, only one reply came. Two simple words from Noah, ringing with a glorious, tyrannical clarity.
"Fuck off."
BOOM!
Tatiana's eyes flashed with lividity.

"Due to the immense respect and decorum that I have for Order, I am holding myself back right now from this very clear disrespect. I ask once more, do not speak on behalf of THE Living Order. I wish to have this dialogue with nobody else other than THE Living Order."
She waited. The silence stretched. And then, again, the same two words, in the same grand, glorious, tyrannical voice.
"Fuck off."
BOOM!
Oh!
Oh!
Tatiana had reached the end of her patience. "We are a solution to the abomination that is THE Loom," she stated, her voice now a cold, flat pronouncement.

"That solution is to grant all living existences on this side of The Veil the blessing of becoming like us. This was a mercy designed by THE Creature and THE Dead Order, and we will now proceed in carrying it out."

"Alongside this will be the procurement and safe obtainment of THE Living Order, who seems to have been taken captive by an entity with intentions that do not align with THE Creature or with Order itself. With respect to the Order that we continue to hold in high regard... we will now begin our operation to rescue you from the clutches of this entity."

chapters.title: Chapter 4326 A Glorious Protocol! I
paragraphs: A terrifying progression.
In existence, there are good enemies, and there are horrid enemies. A good enemy is a straightforward thing.
They want your land, your resources, your head on a spike. They make their intentions clear, and they attack you. You fight, you win or you lose. It is a clean, honest, and brutal transaction.

But a horrid enemy... a horrid enemy is a different beast entirely. They are the ones who attack you while telling you they are doing it for your own good. To save you. To make sure you do not harm yourself.

They are the ones who will burn your house to the ground and then explain, with a sad, paternalistic smile, that they were simply trying to keep you warm. These types of enemies... they are absolutely the worst.
In the Early Veiled Shore.
A profound stillness had settled over the Radiant Shore. The joyous, chaotic energy of progression had given way to a quiet, focused solemnity.
Across the golden sands, Noah's people had emerged from their states of rapid, endowment-fueled cultivation.
Sigrid rose, her form a beacon of pure white Order against the azure backdrop of the Shore. Noah turned to her, a faint, almost teasing smile on his lips. "Are you my captive?"

She looked at him, and her eyes, which held the serene, unyielding light of a fundamental law, flashed with a flicker of something almost like... annoyance. "It doesn't seem like I am," she said, her voice a calm, even current.
"But these existences..." Her gaze drifted to the screens, to the silent, orderly legions of The Prime Dead, and a shadow of concern crossed her perfect features.
Noah saw it, that flicker of worry, and his smile softened. "They are merely Prime Dead," he said, his voice a quiet, reassuring anchor in the sea of her unspoken fears. "Nothing too crazy."
In the next moment, a new presence made itself known.

Khor floated towards him, her diminutive form a stark, beautiful contrast to the vast, open expanse of the Shore, her abyssal eyes pulsing with a contained, ancient power. She turned and looked across the Shore, her gaze settling on the far corner where a second, identical body of herself was calmly overseeing the separation of Bob from the Mutated In Abitability, with Liora standing nearby, her face a mask of anxious, hopeful anticipation.

Khor looked at all of this, then turned back to Noah. "I need to let loose, Outsider," she said, her voice a low, dangerous purr. "I am holding a little anger inside of me, and it would be good to express it. With how much I have been eating... I could likely keep that Tatiana busy. Though she is not a simple one, as she appears. You would have to find a way to deal with the other ones."

Noah smiled at her words. Yes, out of all the impossible, terrible weapons in his arsenal, Khor was undoubtedly one of the strongest. With his power, her power, and the overwhelming might of the Resplendent Citadels, they might just be able to hold back this terrifying new force.
But...
Noah shook his head.

He stared at Khor, at his people, at the magnificent, terrible army he had built, and his smile widened into a grand, tyrannical expression. "You all have gotten a glimpse of My Way. My Civilization. I now wish to give you... a full look at it."
BOOM!
A full look!

Khor was astonished. She looked at him, at the quiet, unshakeable confidence in his eyes, and she realized, with a shock that was a profound, almost delightful thing, that against an enemy that was three, perhaps four times more powerful than him, he was denying her help. Why? Could his Way of Existence be that terrifying?
His Complexity and Purity was only at approximately one Quintillion, while Tatiana alone exceeded four Quintillion, and there were others behind her at three Quintillion and two Quintillion.
Nearly all those he stood against were more powerful than him.
"Are you sure, Outsider?" she asked, her voice a mixture of genuine concern and a deep, ancient curiosity.
Noah smiled and nodded. "Yes. Watch My Way of Existence. Watch My Way of the Mana Architect. Watch My Civilization... and try to hold on strong to your Hunger."
He spoke the words with a grand, almost playful, authority. Khor shook her head with a look of pure, unadulterated incredulity. "You are insane, Outsider."
At that moment, Noah smiled. He closed his eyes and sent his will to RUIN/EDEN.
'Are the Mana Arcana Glyphs I told you to design ready?'
Yes. Mana Arcana Glyphs!

In the Earliest Folds, he had only forged the Mana Glyph of the Primordial Fireball that dealt half a Quintillion in damage and the Mana Arcana Glyph: Annihilation's First Spark that dealt 1.5 Quintillion damage.
But his body had still remained in the Earliest Folds this whole time, and in the hours that had passed there, it had been very, very productive.
Endless Mana had been used to forge an arsenal of the most powerful Mana Arcana Glyphs he could imagine, Glyphs that would allow him to truly express just how terrifying his Way of Existence was!
Because his strength and the strength of his System, at the end of the day, lay in Mana. Infinite Mana.
And for something others did not have, how could he use it best? The answer was terrifyingly clear!
Otherd had limitations of Everythings and much more, but he...did not!
"Show me."
His existence buzzed as he gave the command to RUIN/EDEN, and in the quiet, internal sanctum of his mind, a glorious, terrible presentation began.
|Project: [One Man Army] is complete, Master. Multiple new Mana Arcana Glyphs have been added to your Codex. Allow me to begin the demonstration.|
In his mind's eye, the radiant, card-like structure of the Annihilation's First Spark bloomed into existence.
On its surface, a magnificent, nine-headed Primordial Mana-Flame Wyrm slept, its azure scales shimmering with a contained, apocalyptic power!

|Description: 'From the smallest spark, the greatest inferno is born.' This Arcana summons a [Primordial Mana-Flame Wyrm], a being of pure, conceptual fire forged from your own, infinite essence. The Wyrm unleashes a single, guided torrent of annihilating azure flame.|
|Cost: 1 Unit of [Everythings of Mana].|
|Requirements to Cast: Must be the Architect of Mana.|

|Effect: Due to its rarity, it deals 1.5 Quintillion in pure, untyped Mana-based damage that ignores all known resistances and authorities. The attack is conceptually 'true' and cannot be dodged. Its capabilities will advance and scale upwards as you progress.|
|Cooldown: 1 Second.|
The illusory image of the first card moved to the side, and a new one floated into view.
On its surface was a glorious, azure-furred beast, a Mellivora benfieldi, an ancient honey badger, its eyes blazing with a defiant, almost comical, indifference.
|[Mana Arcana Glyph: The Indomitable Will]|
|School: Mana (Primordial)|
|Rarity: Primordial|

|Description: 'Existence is a relentless, brutal assault. This Arcana simply... does not care.' Summons the conceptual form of an Ancient Honey Badger, a being whose very nature is a defiant rejection of all external influence. The Badger floats above the caster, a silent, furry guardian of pure, unadulterated stubbornness.|
|Cost: 1 Unit of [Everythings of Mana].|
|Requirements to Cast: Must be the Architect of Mana.|

|Effect: For one minute, you are protected by a [Badger's Barrier of Mana], a shield capable of absorbing up to 1.5 Quintillion in damage from any source. As they say... a honey badger does not give a damn.|
|Cooldown: 1 Second.|
Noah's mind buzzed as he looked at its full details. He nodded once. "Let's see the next ones."
The presentation continued, a pageant of impossible, beautiful, and utterly broken tools of war.
|[Mana Arcana Glyph: The Unshakeable Mountain]|
|School: Mana (Primordial)|
|Rarity: Primordial|

|Description: 'The storm rages, the winds howl, but the mountain remains.' This Arcana summons not a creature, but a concept: a spectral, azure mountain range that surrounds the caster, a fortress of pure, unyielding stability.|
|Cost: 1 Unit of [Everythings of Mana].|
|Requirements to Cast: Must be the Architect of Mana.|

|Effect: Grants the [Mountain's Heart] aura for one minute. All incoming attacks are reduced by 1 Quintillion in power. This is a flat reduction, not a percentage. Small attacks are simply... negated.|
|Cooldown: 1 Second.|
|[Mana Arcana Glyph: The Tyrant's Maw]|
|School: Mana (Primordial)|
|Rarity: Primordial|
|Description: 'The ocean is not just water; it is a mouth.' Summons the conceptual ghost of a Megalodon, its form a shimmering, azure vortex of pure, predatory hunger.|
|Cost: 1 Unit of [Everythings of Mana].|
|Requirements to Cast: Must be the Architect of Mana.|
|Effect: For one minute, all of your attacks deal 50% more damage. This is a conceptual amplification; your very intent to harm is made more potent.|
|Cooldown: 1 Second.|
|[Mana Arcana Glyph: The Saber's Edge]|
|School: Mana (Primordial)|
|Rarity: Primordial|
|Description: 'There is no defense against a perfect cut.' Summons the ephemeral spirit of a Smilodon, its azure fangs long, sharp, and impossibly, conceptually, true.|
|Cost: 1 Unit of [Everythings of Mana].|
|Requirements to Cast: Must be the Architect of Mana.|
|Effect: For one minute, all of your attacks gain a base damage of 1 Quintillion. This damage is applied before all other multipliers and ignores all resistances.|
|Cooldown: 1 Second.|
|[Mana Arcana Glyph: The Unbreakable Shell]|
|School: Mana (Primordial)|
|Rarity: Primordial|
|Description: 'The best offense is an impenetrable defense.' Summons the spectral carapace of an ancient Ankylosaurus, a living fortress of azure, crystalline plates.|
|Cost: 1 Unit of [Everythings of Mana].|
|Requirements to Cast: Must be the Architect of Mana.|
|Effect: For one minute, all incoming damage is reduced by 25%.|
|Cooldown: 1 Second.|
|[Mana Arcana Glyph: The Unbound Moment]|
|School: Mana (Primordial)|
|Description: 'Time is a river. This Arcana is a dam.' Summons a glorious, spectral Wheel of Existence, its azure form spinning with the light of a billion frozen moments.|
|Rarity: Primordial|
|Cost: 1 Unit of [Everythings of Mana].|
|Requirements to Cast: Must be the Architect of Mana.|
|Effect: For one minute, all of your abilities, including your Mana Arcana Glyphs, have no cooldown.|
|Cooldown: 1 Second.|

Noah looked at the glorious, terrible arsenal that had been laid out before him in the quiet of his own mind. A one-second cooldown. He could, theoretically, have them all active at once. He could become a walking, talking, and utterly unbreakable apocalypse!
And he even went further to give a big middle finger to cooldowns with another terrifying Arcana!
Oh!
"Okay," he said, his voice a quiet, satisfied hum. "The Codex is coming along nicely. Let us go and show others what the Way of Mana truly means, okay?"
Being overpowered.
Many...misunderstand the very idea of this concept itself!
It's like the difference between imagining being rich (yacht parties and endless vacation) versus actually being rich (mostly tax documents and people asking for money).

Most believe being overpowered means winning every fight, solving every problem with a gesture, having Existence bend to your whims. They imagine it as freedom from consequence, the ultimate power fantasy where you're basically playing life with cheat codes enabled.
This...was a fundamental misunderstanding of the burden of being overpowered!

Some say that truly overpowered beings understand something the power-seekers don't: strength isn't freedom- it's prison. The stronger you become, the smaller your world gets. Every increase in power is a decrease in things that can matter to you.

This is why truly overpowered beings often become either utterly detached or desperately attached to tiny, trivial things. THE Creature playing with Early Creatures and Fold Dwellers like pets. THE Living Paradox obsessing over THE Creature!
Some overpowered beings cling to whatever can still provide meaning in an existence that has become tissue paper to their touch.
What it truly means to be overpowered is to be disconnected from the very fabric of existence you sought to master.
It was winning so thoroughly that there's no game left to play. It's being so strong that strength itself...becomes meaningless.
Some believe that those who are genuinely overpowered don't seek more power. They seek limitations, weaknesses, something...anything, that can make them feel connected to existence again.
The goal of becoming overpowered is to never have to struggle again.
But struggle...is what gives existence meaning.

So when someone says they want to be overpowered, what they really mean is they want to be just powerful enough to overcome their current problems. Actually being overpowered? Well...this was hard to conceptualize!

chapters.title: Chapter 4328 A Glorious Protocol! III
paragraphs: In the isolated bubble where Noah, Schrodinger, and Leonore Rureaux were meeting.
POP!
The small, world-sized isolated domain popped like a soap bubble, its blue-gold light scattering into the chaotic void of Collapse.

Noah began to float up, his figure a slow, deliberate ascent into the heart of the storm. His presence immediately came under the gazes of Tatiana and the Prime Dead, who had been waiting with a profound, terrible patience. Their collective authority, a silent, crushing weight, began to buzz with a new, focused power.
From the small garden he had just left, Schrodinger frowned, his usual playful demeanor gone, replaced by a mask of genuine concern.
"What exactly could you be doing, friend?" he shouted, his voice a sharp, cutting blade of disbelief. "I did not take you for someone on a suicide mission..."
Noah ignored the words. He continued his ascent, a silent, tyrannical king rising to meet a challenge.
He came to a stop at the same level as Tatiana, the two of them now facing each other across a chasm of silent, simmering hostility.
It was a glorious, terrible standoff. And in the periphery of this cosmic duel, a quiet, almost comical, exodus was underway.
The Living Existences who had remained conscious, beings who could command the very fabric of reality, were now engaged in a desperate, silent retreat.
They pulled along their unconscious comrades, their movements a frantic, chaotic scramble to get as far away from this impending cataclysm as possible.
They did not run; they scurried, their usual regal dignity replaced by the primal, undeniable urge to simply... not be here!

Tatiana's gaze, cold and sharp as a shard of obsidian, swept over Noah, a slow, dismissive up-and-down assessment. "Are you the one," she asked, her voice the sound of a tombstone cracking, "who has been disrespectfully replying on behalf of THE Living Order and holding her captive?"

Noah gazed back at her, at the legion of Prime Dead Early Creatures that were beginning to rise on the vessel behind her, at the hundreds of obsidian-white Dead Existential Armors that were now lighting up, their dead eyes glowing with a cold, malevolent light.
"I'm the one who has been telling you to fuck off," he replied, his voice not a shout, but a low, resonant, and utterly absolute pronouncement. "But you cannot seem to get the message."
His words were a physical weight in the dead air. Tatiana's eyes pulsed with a dangerous, crimson light. But Noah was not done.

"Are you the same Tatiana who held a concentrated Everything of THE Creature?" he asked, his tone now a blade of pure, condescending curiosity. "You seem a bit weak compared to others of your stature, like Gilgamesh... is this a lesser body of yours, or did you simply not live up to the potential you were born with? You were not defective... right?"
BOOM!
The words were a calculated, tyrannical cruelty, a series of precise, surgical strikes aimed at the very heart of her pride. And in response, Tatiana smiled.
"Okay."
A single word. She didn't curse. She didn't bellow in rage. She simply said, "Okay," and the very fabric of the collapsed space trembled.
A brilliant, pristine white light of Order began to pulse around her, and woven within it, a deep, obsidian grandeur, the unmistakable signature of a Principle, began to bloom.
The moment that terrifying display of aura began, Noah's eyes flashed with a cold, almost bored, light. "Activate the One Man Army Protocol."
One Man Army. He named it this because other entities, even the great and terrible beings of the Earliest Folds, had their limits.
They had to expend their Everythings, a finite, precious resource, to unleash their most terrifying capabilities. This limitation... his existence did not even register it.
He had Infinite Mana. And his most terrifying capabilities, his Mana Arcana Glyphs... all ran on Mana.
In the next instant, a glorious, swirling storm of stellar blue brilliance erupted around him. The first Mana Arcana Glyph was cast.
|[The Indomitable Will] has been activated.|
A wave of pure, boundless Mana, an ocean of it, surged from his small figure. It coalesced above him, forming a creature of impossible, glorious defiance.

It was a Mellivora benfieldi, an ancient honey badger, its form now a shimmering, spectral azure. Its eyes were two cold, arrogant stars, and they gazed out at Tatiana and her legion with a look of profound, absolute indifference.

|The conceptual form of an Ancient Honey Badger has been summoned. It is a being whose very nature is a defiant rejection of all external influence. For one minute, you are protected by a [Badger's Barrier of Mana], a shield capable of absorbing up to 1.5 Quintillion in damage. As they say... a honey badger does not give a damn.|
A shimmering, azure barrier, its surface a swirling, chaotic vortex of pure, unyielding will, formed around Noah. But the symphony of his power had only just begun.
|Master, the other Mana Arcana Glyphs under the [One Man Army Protocol] are being activated.|
|[The Unbound Moment] has been cast.|
|[The Tyrant's Maw] has been cast.|
|[The Unbreakable Shell] has been cast.|
|[The Saber's Edge] has been cast.|
|[The Unshakeable Mountain] has been cast.|
Above him, the azure badger was joined by a pantheon of impossible, beautiful, and utterly terrifying manifestations.
A glorious, spectral Wheel of Existence, its azure form spinning with the light of a billion frozen moments, appeared, its presence a declaration that time itself was now his to command.
The conceptual ghost of a Megalodon, its form a shimmering, azure vortex of pure, predatory hunger, materialized, its silent roar a promise of a feast to come!
A spectral carapace of an ancient Ankylosaurus, a living fortress of azure, crystalline plates, formed a second, denser layer of defense around him!
HUUM!
The ephemeral spirit of a Smilodon, its azure fangs long, sharp, and impossibly, conceptually, true, materialized, its silent roar a promise of a perfect, unavoidable cut.
And finally, a vast, spectral mountain range, a fortress of pure, unyielding stability, rose behind him, its peaks scraping against the very firmament of the Fold.

He was a glorious, terrible sight. The entire region around him was now a roiling sea of his Mana, and from its depths, these six colossal, illusory manifestations glared out at his enemies, a council of primordial titans ready to dispense judgment!
OOOOH!
|Finalizing Protocol...|
|All buffs are now active.|
| - [The Unbound Moment]: For one minute, all of your abilities, including your Mana Arcana Glyphs, have no cooldown.|
| - [The Tyrant's Maw]: For one minute, all of your attacks deal 50% more damage.|
| - [The Unbreakable Shell]: For one minute, all incoming damage is reduced by 25%.|
| - [The Saber's Edge]: For one minute, all of your attacks gain a base damage of 1 Quintillion.|
| - [The Unshakeable Mountain]: For one minute, all incoming attacks are reduced by 1 Quintillion in power.|
| - [The Indomitable Will]: A barrier of 1.5 Quintillion stands ready to absorb all harm.|
The final summary bloomed, a stark, numerical declaration of his new, impossible reality.
|One Man Army Protocol: Status Update.|
|Active Buffs: 6.|

|Defensive Capacity: Your [Mana-Born Aegis of the Architect] and its [Innate Omnichalcum Aura Field] provide a base defense of 920 Quadrillion. The [Badger's Barrier of Mana] adds a 1.5 Quintillion buffer. [The Unshakeable Mountain] provides a flat 1 Quintillion reduction to all incoming attacks. [The Unbreakable Shell] provides a 25% reduction to all damage that bypasses these defenses.|

|Total Defensive Threshold: You can currently withstand a single, instantaneous blow of approximately 4.5+ Quintillion in power, or a sustained assault of a lesser, but still astronomical, magnitude.|

|Offensive Capacity: Your base power of 1 Quintillion, amplified by [The Saber's Edge] to a base of 2 Quintillion, is then further amplified by 50% through [The Tyrant's Maw]. Your every attack will now carry a base damage of 4.5 Quintillion. All of this, with no cooldowns for the next minute.|

chapters.title: Chapter 4329 MANA! I
paragraphs: The scene was a paradox of glorious, terrible power.

A single, defiant figure stood wreathed in a sea of his own boundless Mana, surrounded by a pantheon of six colossal, spectral guardians. Before him, an army of endings waited, their silent, orderly ranks a testament to a power that had transcended the chaos of death!

In the span of an instant, a silent, lightning-fast conversation, a torrent of pure, conceptual data, flashed between Tatiana and the Prime Dead Early Creatures behind her as they communicated together simultaneously!
Tatiana's thoughts were a blade of cold, precise logic.

"The enemy is utilizing a system similar to our own Living Astral Codex. The manifestations are potent, but they are temporary. All such abilities have a cost, a cooldown. He has played his hand too early."
Valerius, his half-skeletal face a mask of regal amusement, sent his own thoughts in reply.

"His power is impressive, for a fleeting moment. His Codex must be of a high grade, but it cannot be limitless. He may have ten, perhaps twenty Arcana at his disposal. Once their timers run out, he will be a firefly against a sun."
Tatiana's mind was a whirlwind of calculation as she nodded.

"He who is hasty in the hunt, who shows his full strength at the first rustle of leaves, will find his arrows spent when the true beast emerges from the shadows. The patient hunter, who waits, who observes, who understands that time is a weapon... he is the one who feasts."

She paused, a flicker of something almost like caution in her thoughts. "But treat this one with extreme care. He was capable of capturing and restraining THE Living Order. That is not the mark of a fool."
HUUM!
Another of the Prime Dead, a being whose form was a beautiful, grotesque fusion of bone and shadow, interjected.
"And what of The Living Order, Ashen Queen? If he falls, what is our protocol for her?"

Tatiana's reply was a cold, absolute command. "While I hold him down, I will give the word. You will penetrate that protective domain. You will procure THE Living Order. And you will treat them with the respect they are due. They are a prize, not a prisoner."
The Prime Dead nodded in silent, unified assent. The plan was set. Tatiana's gaze, now a thing of pure, unadulterated focus, settled on the defiant, flame-wreathed figure across the void.
"Child," she asked, her voice a demeaning, almost bored, inquiry, "what is your name?"

Noah did not answer. He simply stared at her, his expression a cold, unreadable mask. The six glorious, tyrannical manifestations behind him... the Badger, the Mountain, the Wheel, the Shark, the Saber Cat, the Shell... they stared back at her, their collective gaze a silent, crushing weight.
She did not wait for a reply she knew would not come.

She changed her tactics, her voice now a sharp, probing question. "Early Creature, what is your name? How did you get your hands on a Codex after the purge? Do you know that your actions are going against your Ancestor right now? Against THE Creature?"
She knew the words were a potent weapon. All Early Creatures, in their own way, held a deep, almost instinctual, reverence for THE Creature. What was this one's Origin? His Lineage?
But the entity opposite her simply looked on, his expression one of arrogant, almost pitying, amusement.

"I'll be sure to check with my Lineage," he said, his voice a low, dangerous hum that was more terrifying than any shout, "but I can't recall any time THE Creature came down to give a damn about me or anyone else. But... I truly don't feel like talking right now. You talked a damn lot earlier. I feel like fighting right now. I feel like killing."
Tatiana smiled at his words. She laughed. A silent, terrible, and utterly genuine laugh.

At her amusement, the legion behind her moved. The Prime Dead Early Creatures and the few hundred Dead Existential Armors began to line up, a billowing, obsidian wave of absolute, ordered power against a single, defiant entity.

"You don't feel like fighting because you have hastily used up your Arcana and they will expire soon," she said, her voice a condescending, almost instructional, lecture. "Use up a few more, and you will be done. All you will have left will be your Haki, your Glyphs, and your Complexity. This is why you feel like fighting right away. I thought of wasting time to put your Arcana to waste, but let me stretch my muscles here a bit. I haven't truly moved around in a while."
At her words, a billowing, obsidian light erupted from her, covering the right half of her body completely.
Her entire figure was now wreathed in shimmering, obsidian flames. She closed her eyes, and she felt her power.
Her Existence. Her Way.
Her Way was... the Way of Dreams.
She was a Dreamer. She was THE Creature's very Dream. And she... was mighty.
BOOM!
In the next moment, the already terrifying power radiating from Tatiana rumbled, and when she opened her eyes again, her entire aura, her very complexity, had more than doubled.
Doubled!
For this was her Way. This was her Principle.
The Principle of the Waking Dream!
A Principle that allowed the wielder to pull the 'dreamed' or 'ideal' version of their own existence into reality, superimposing it upon their current form!
It was an act of making a potential future into an absolute present.
And this was her Dream. Her Way.
She opened her eyes. The left was its usual, cold, crimson light. But the right... the right was now a swirling, obsidian-gold vortex, a gateway into a realm of pure, untamed dreams.
She looked at the defiant figure who had dared to keep THE Living Order from her, and she whispered, her voice a final, absolute verdict.
"I won't even transform you. You... are not deserving of such a blessing."
She took a single, graceful step. "Do you understand?"
She said the words not from across the void, but from inches away from Noah, her form having crossed the impossible distance in an instant.
She was there, a queen of dreams and death, her power a suffocating, absolute presence.
But shockingly... the entity surrounded by a sea of mana was already looking at her, his expression calm, his gaze cold!
Even her Quintillions of Complexity and Purity that had just erupted from her... he did not seem phased!
Oh!
